round1.proposed_rule: Give one entry per dataset the report distinguishes. When a dataset is built by merging or linking sources, give one entry per source. A dataset whose setting is not stated gets the value 'not_reported'. The item status stays reported if any dataset's setting is stated. Code a category only when the report names the institution or programme that collected the data (a survey, hospital, clinic, registry, cohort, or a public agency's case records), and follow it with the printed phrase. Describing only the patients or the content of the records (e.g. a mention of patients' clinical tests, 'medical records', 'physical checkups') with no collecting institution or programme named is not_reported for that dataset; quote the phrase in the rationale. Any department or outpatient clinic of a named hospital is 'hospital'. Use 'clinic' only for a stand-alone clinic or practice. Records compiled by a public agency that are not a survey, registry or cohort are 'other'. A distribution platform (e.g. Kaggle, a data repository) is not a setting.

Classify an explicitly named outpatient clinic as clinic even when hospital-affiliated; retain multiple categories only when multiple collection settings are explicitly stated for a dataset. Clinical activities, data contents, compilers and repositories alone do not establish a collection setting: record not_reported; use other only for a stated setting outside the listed categories. Give one entry per dataset the report distinguishes, recording not_reported where its setting is unstated, and never add datasets or setting details absent from the printed text.

round1.proposed_rule: List every stated removal of participants or records from a dataset used to develop or validate the model in the main analysis. This includes restrictions worded as inclusion criteria, survey-year exclusions, complete-case removal and outlier removal; record each restriction as its complement (e.g. 'aged ≤20 excluded'). Do not list removal of variables or features, resampling for class balance, subsets used for only one model, or removals used only in sensitivity or comparison analyses; put these in the rationale. Give n as printed. If the report prints exact totals immediately before and after one named step, n = before − after (kind derived, with the formula). If the totals span several steps, give one combined n naming all those criteria, with each criterion's own n not_reported. Never split a combined n using other numbers, and never derive n from approximate or unprinted totals. A figure count with no criterion label is not a criterion; mention it in the rationale.

For each dataset, record stated participant/record exclusions or explicit eligibility restrictions, preserving the printed eligibility wording and any model-specific, comparison or undersampling scope; feature deletion, reformatting and unspecified cleaning do not themselves supply participant-exclusion criteria. Record excluded n only where printed and linked to that criterion or combined group; otherwise use n = not_reported, without subtracting retained totals or allocating combined counts to individual criteria. Use an unlabelled number only if its role as an exclusion count is established, with criterion = not_reported. Stated criteria make the item reported even when counts are missing. Use only supplied evidence and apply the existing same-fact, same-object, same-condition test for inconsistency: a numerical gap or omitted step alone does not establish a contradiction or an additional exclusion.

Do not list (mention in the rationale): removal of variables or features, reformatting, resampling for class balance, subsets used by only one model, and removals used only in sensitivity or comparison analyses. When such totals span several steps, give one combined n naming those criteria, and each criterion's own n is not_reported. In all other cases n = not_reported. Never split a combined n. round1.proposed_rule: Core: which outcome was modelled. This means the target variable, and its classes or scale, named in the text or in the title, legend or axis of a figure or table that belongs to a model. If the outcome is named, status is reported. A criterion, cutoff or class-assignment rule that is not printed is its own value entry 'not_reported'. Status is unclear only when the modelled target can be inferred only from the study aim or the result distributions. Give one entry per distinct printed definition. Each entry contains the whole defining phrase, including its cutoffs and classes. Where datasets or analyses use different printed definitions, give separate entries. Never carry criteria from one dataset or analysis to another. A definition that is reused in a secondary analysis is one entry, and the unit names the analyses that use it. A different variable, scale or cutoff in a secondary analysis is a new entry labelled as such. Categories or risk groups derived from the fitted model's output are part of the outcome entry, not separate outcomes. Record inconsistency only for the outcome definition itself.

Extract the printed definition for each explicitly modelled outcome, including secondary and sensitivity outcomes; distinguish definitions where the report states they differ, without creating additional outcomes for repeated models, descriptive groups or post-modelling node labels. An identified modelled variable or set of classes is reported, with missing definition details recorded as not_reported; use unclear when what was modelled cannot be fixed from the text. Use only the supplied report evidence: do not infer targets from aims or matching counts, extend definitions beyond their stated scope, supply unstated complementary cutoffs, repair printed inequalities, or rely on coder descriptions of unavailable text. Assess inconsistency separately using two supported statements about the same fact, object and condition; wording, notation, rounding, explicitly stated exceptions and counts of different objects do not by themselves establish contradictory outcome definitions.

round1.proposed_rule: Code a step here only if the report states that it addresses class imbalance or class balance, or names a standard imbalance method (SMOTE/ADASYN, minority oversampling, majority undersampling, class weights inversely proportional to class frequency, threshold moving for imbalance). Some steps change class proportions but the report gives another purpose (data augmentation because a group is small, matching to reduce selection bias, a cutoff or weight chosen to maximise sensitivity at evaluation). These steps are not imbalance handling. If nothing else qualifies, status is not_reported and the step is described in the rationale. Noting that classes are imbalanced, without a stated method, is also not_reported. Data scope: training only when the report says so; whole data when the cited text says balancing was applied to the full analysis pool from which the modelling sample was drawn, or done before any split; otherwise not_stated.

Count explicitly described class-specific sampling or synthetic augmentation that sets or changes class representation in the modelling data, including matching at a specified class ratio and equal additions to initially unequal classes, regardless of its stated purpose; record the operation without attributing an unstated motive. Class counts or outcome recoding alone do not establish handling. When a potentially eligible weight or cutoff procedure is mentioned but its role cannot be determined, code unclear and quote the ambiguous text without assigning a method. Record data scope separately for each method: sample-selection descriptions alone do not establish timing relative to a split, and unspecified scope remains not stated; keep unspecified model allocation at study level. Establish inconsistency only from contradictory supplied statements about the same fact, object and condition.

final_rule:
Record training-stage imbalance methods, including class/sample weighting and threshold moving, and explicitly described class-specific sampling or synthetic augmentation that changes the training class distribution, regardless of stated purpose; record the operation and separately whether imbalance is a stated purpose. Record data scope separately for each method (training only / whole data / not stated), without inferring timing from sample-selection descriptions, and retain study-level allocation when models are unspecified.

Exceptions:
- Augmentation that leaves the class distribution unchanged, class counts alone, and outcome merging or redefinition do not establish imbalance handling.

round1.proposed_rule: Give one entry for each evaluation whose performance values are printed (text, table or figure). Do not give an entry for a split or validation set that is described but has no printed results; mention it in the rationale. Take the type from the evaluation's own title, legend, label or text. If there is none, apply a general statement of the study's single evaluation design (e.g. 'for evaluating the models we split the data 80/20'). If no such link exists, or more than one stated design could apply, the type is 'not_stated' (kind judged). Never link an evaluation by matching values or counts in another place. Code apparent when the evaluation is stated to be on the data the model was fitted on, or when its printed n or counts equal the sample the model was fitted on or include the training data (e.g. resubstitution, a table of the whole sample, a lift chart of all participants). Bootstrap or cross-validation gives its own entry only when the report presents that resampling as an evaluation with its own printed estimates. This includes CV scores that are reported as results, even if the same CV was used for tuning. Bootstrap used only for CIs of another evaluation's estimates takes that evaluation's type. Values deleted or masked on purpose and then predicted from the remaining data are split_sample (state the repetitions).

For each model × dataset evaluation with printed performance values, classify the design using statements that link those estimates to the evaluation data or procedure; a general method applies wherever its stated scope covers the evaluation, without requiring repetition. Keep separately reported evaluation results separate: repeated random hold-outs are split_sample; resampling explicitly reported as performance evaluation counts even when also used for tuning or stability, whereas tuning-only cross-validation or bootstrap confidence intervals alone do not add a validation type. Do not add evaluations merely because a procedure is described, and do not infer their designs or provenance from matching numbers, sample totals, plot axes, fold labels alone, artificial missingness or a different dataset name. Where an evaluation exists but its design cannot be fixed, record that missing or unclear design separately while retaining reported status for answered evaluations. Apply the existing same-fact, same-object, same-condition test for inconsistency: coexisting procedures need not conflict, and contradictory performance values do not themselves establish contradictory validation designs.

round1.proposed_rule: If the report states that a validation or test set is part of the same dataset as the training data (a split, hold-out, 'portion of the data', or a subset defined by some criterion) and does not state random allocation, code status reported with value 'none (split of the same data)'. Add the basis in brackets only if it is printed (e.g. 'stratified', 'cases with missing outcome'). Write 'random' only when the report states it. This also applies when the data pool several years or regions, unless the report states that allocation was by year or place. Do not code a split of one dataset as 'temporal' or 'geographic', and do not use not_stated or not_reported when the report states that the test set comes from the same data. Use not_stated only when the report does not say where the validation or test data come from. Judge separation against the data the model was developed on. Code 'temporal' only when the printed periods do not overlap. Code 'geographic: <places as printed>' when the places differ, even if the periods overlap. Resampling that is used only for tuning or recalibration, including recalibration within an external set, does not create a separate unit and does not change that set's value.

Give one entry per stated validation/test dataset, comparing it with the data used to fit the model or recalibration being evaluated; tuning-only cross-validation and captions that do not identify folds do not establish additional evaluation datasets. Record temporal or geographic separation only when the cited periods or places establish it; shared source dates or overlapping periods do not establish temporal separation, and common-source, unspecified, stratified or nonresponse-based partitions alone establish neither randomness nor absence of geographic separation. Use 'none (random split of the same data)' when random allocation, including random outcome masking, is established, and 'none (cross-validation)' for stated cross-validation of the development data; otherwise use 'not_stated', applying the existing not_reported/unclear distinction. Retain any established dimension when the other is unstated, and never use not_applicable when validation/test data exist.

round1.proposed_rule: Core: the intended use of the study's prediction model. Give two study-level entries. The first starts 'use:' and quotes, kind printed, each phrase the report uses to state what the model is for. The second starts 'users:' and quotes the persons the report names as using or acting on the model's predictions. If no users are named, the second entry is 'users: not_reported'. Persons count as intended users only when the cited sentence links them to the prediction or the tool, not to the disease in general. If the report states purposes for different populations or outcomes (for example a different age group or condition), record each as printed. Then set inconsistency to present and cite both places in the note. Status stays reported.

Record intended-use phrases explicitly attributed to the study, including anomalous aims; do not infer from a topic mismatch that a statement concerns another study. Copy only wording present in the supplied text. Record intended users when stated or clearly implied; an inferred user classification is judged and must be supported by the printed phrase describing their role.

round2.revised_rule: Record, kind printed, every phrase the report attributes to this study or its model as its purpose, even one naming a population or outcome the study did not analyse. Do not drop such a phrase on the guess that it belongs to another study. Copy only wording in the supplied text. Record as intended users the persons the cited text links to using or acting on the model's predictions, not to the disease in general. Their kind is printed, or judged only when a printed phrase about their role clearly implies them. If none are stated, record users as not_reported. When two places give conflicting purposes or target populations for the same study or model, set inconsistency to present and cite both places. Purposes that only list several outcomes or uses are not a conflict.

round1.proposed_rule: Final model(s) = the model(s) the report recommends, deploys or names as final. If several are final (e.g. one per sex), give separate entries only where the inputs differ, and name the model or subgroup in the unit. Inputs = the variables the report states were entered into that model. A feature-importance ranking (top-k) is the input set only if the report says the model uses only those features. Inputs of unsupervised clustering or phenotyping steps are not prediction inputs. If the report does not let you identify the final model's inputs or input groups, status is unclear: give only the intended-setting entry and name the candidate variables in the rationale. Intended setting: copy (kind printed) the stated setting, users, time of use and target population of use, or give 'not_stated'. Collection method 'evident from the variable itself' applies only to physical measurements and specimen tests: measured height, weight, waist or BMI -> body measurement; blood pressure -> blood pressure measurement; spirometry values -> pulmonary function test; analytes -> blood test or urine test when the variable name or the report's grouping names the specimen, otherwise 'laboratory test (specimen not_stated)'. All kind judged. Demographic, socioeconomic, behavioural, history, diagnosis, symptom and self-rating variables are not evident: record 'not_stated' unless the report says how that variable or its named group was collected. A general statement about the survey or dataset (questionnaire, interview, CAPI, 'self-reported data') is applied to a predictor group only if it names that group or domain (a table section heading or survey-domain name counts); otherwise 'not_stated', with the statement quoted in the rationale.

Record the stated intended setting/time, or 'not_stated', and acquisition only for predictor groups supported as inputs of the final model(s) offered for use; candidates and separate analyses require a stated link, an importance ranking does not establish an exhaustive or reduced input set, and best performance alone does not establish that only one model is offered. Record acquisition at the level stated or evident from the variable itself, including a broad measurement or examination type when its detailed protocol is absent; otherwise use 'not_stated', without inferring collection from a demographic label, an ambiguous abbreviation, or membership in a mixed survey. An answered acquisition item remains reported when the setting, other groups, or completeness of the input list is missing; use unclear when the core information itself cannot be fixed, and do not fill gaps with presumed inputs. Copy wording exactly for printed values and classify acquisition categories as judged; record inconsistency only for contradictory statements about the same fact, object and condition, without changing status.

round1.proposed_rule: List only data-dependent steps the report describes. A step is data-dependent when its result is estimated from the analysed data: imputation, scaling, learned features (PCA or factor analysis, k-means groups, data-based cut-points or IQR outlier limits), data-driven predictor selection (including filtering by missingness), matching, resampling or class weighting, hyperparameter tuning, a stated choice of model, number of predictors or threshold, and recalibration. Do not list fixed-rule recoding or categorisation, formula-derived variables, exclusion of participants by fixed criteria, fixed settings, the fitting of the model itself (including growing or pruning the final tree), or steps the report does not mention. Model or algorithm selection is a step only when the report states that a choice was made from results (e.g. a statement that the best-performing model was chosen). Printing several models' results on a set and naming the best is reporting, not selection. Status is reported when at least one data-dependent step is described (not_stated scopes are allowed), not_reported when none is described, and not_applicable when the study has no validation or test data at all (no split, cross-validation or bootstrap).

Record explicitly described steps, including predictor derivation/recoding and described embedded selection, and logically established nonperformance; complete-case exclusion can establish no imputation, whereas fixed settings or silence establish neither tuning nor its absence. Keep steps, models and final versus resampled fitting distinct: assign scope only when cited statements or explicit figure relationships jointly identify the named step and the relevant data or partition; otherwise use not_stated, retaining any known full-data fitting fact in the rationale without inferring before-split timing. Narrative order, sample or root-node totals, generic cross-validation statements and neighbouring figure labels alone establish neither a step's split/fold scope nor a contradiction with training-only scope. Use test_outcomes_used only when the report establishes that evaluation outcomes informed a choice used before performance on that same set was reported; comparisons, bold maxima and best-model labels alone do not establish this. Status is reported when at least one scope or stated/established nonperformance answers the item, unclear when qualifying steps are described but every scope remains not_stated, and not_reported when no qualifying step or nonperformance is stated.

round1.proposed_rule: Give one entry pair per dataset whose performance is reported (held-out split, temporal or external set; cross-validation folds only if their estimates are reported). Do not give entries for cross-validation used only for tuning or for whole-sample analyses that report no performance. Persons separate = yes only when the report states it: either the split is counted in persons (participants/subjects/patients assigned to each set, or one record per person before the split), or the dataset is described as independent or as separately recruited or collected (another survey cycle or year, institution or data source; kind judged, quote it). A split of 'the data' or 'the dataset', or set sizes that add up to the total, is not_stated. Used for tuning or selection = yes only when the report, including supplementary code, states a step that used this dataset's outcomes before its performance was reported: hyperparameter tuning; threshold choice; recalibration; predictor selection on named data that include this dataset (for CV folds also 'not nested within cross-validation'); or a stated choice of the final or proposed model, algorithm, configuration or number of predictors based on this dataset's results. Naming the best model in a comparison where every compared model's estimate is reported is not selection. Neither are explanations (SHAP, importance) computed on the dataset's inputs. Code 'no' only when the report states that the dataset was not used for development or was used only for final evaluation; 'used for validation' alone is not_stated. Status is reported when at least one entry is yes or no. When every entry is not_stated, status is not_reported (never unclear for that reason), and the split description goes in the rationale.

For each stated validation/test dataset, extract person separation and use for tuning or selection independently, using only statements or linked supplementary code that establish the particular fact for that dataset. Code persons separate as yes only when person-level non-overlap is established, and no when overlap with development or earlier tuning persons is established; dataset labels, dates, sources, row partitions and count arithmetic alone are insufficient. Code used for tuning or selection as yes only when that dataset's outcomes are linked to a stated tuning or selection decision before the reported evaluation, including predictor or algorithm selection and selection of thresholds used for its reported threshold-dependent metrics; a best-performance description alone, test-predictor explanations, or selection outside cross-validation does not establish this link. Code no only when non-use is stated; otherwise enter not_stated, without inventing datasets, procedures or timing. Status is reported if either core fact is established, with the other retained as not_stated when necessary; use not_reported when neither is addressed beyond related information, and unclear when evidence about a core fact is genuinely ambiguous. Preserve contradictory statements about the same dataset and use as inconsistency present without changing reported status.

round1.proposed_rule: Give one value entry per distinct metric, kind judged: the normalised name, then all printed names in parentheses, then ': ' and the definition copied as printed (formula, computing phrase or averaging method), or ': definition not_reported'. If a metric is printed under several names or in several analyses (e.g. cross-validation accuracy, or a value called 'accuracy' that is the balanced-accuracy value), list it once with all its names. Spelling out an abbreviation (e.g. 'area under the ROC curve') is a printed name, not a definition. Confusion-matrix counts are not metrics. If performance numbers are printed but no metric is named, or the printed label does not identify a performance metric, the status is unclear: quote the label in the value. For this item, mark inconsistency only when two places give conflicting names or definitions of the same metric. Value mismatches, including values recomputed from counts, are not recorded here, and neither are label typos or contradictions about the outcome; those go in the items they concern.

Create a study-level inventory of metrics supported by actual printed performance values, excluding axis labels and selection/tuning-only scores; consolidate repeated occurrences of the same metric, retain stated averaging qualifiers, and do not equate distinct labels solely because their values match. Copy supplied name expansions, verbal definitions and formulas without repairing missing notation or supplying standard definitions; mark missing definitions not_reported, and retain confusion-matrix symbols as definition components rather than additional metrics. An explicitly identified nonstandard performance metric may be reported under its printed name without a definition; use unclear when numerical prediction or performance claims leave what was measured unidentified, and not_reported when neither an eligible value nor such an ambiguous numerical claim appears. For this item, flag inconsistency only when supplied statements contradict the same metric definition under the same conditions.

round1.proposed_rule: A stated limitation is a statement in which the authors present a weakness, restriction or caveat of their own study's design, data, predictors, outcome measurement, model or results. It may appear anywhere in the report or supplementary material, not only in a limitations paragraph. A stated need to validate or confirm this model (e.g. a statement that external validation is still needed) counts. These are not limitations: descriptions or explanations of results (e.g. overfitting or miscalibration observed) unless the authors call them a limitation or caveat; general disadvantages of a method type; drawbacks of comparator models used to argue for the proposed model; generic remarks about the field; and future-work plans that do not name a shortcoming of this study. Give one value entry (unit '') per limitation. Use kind 'printed' for a copied phrase and kind 'judged' for a paraphrase. If no such statement exists, status is not_reported; do not use unclear for vague or generic remarks.

List short verbatim phrases wherever the authors state a drawback, constraint, or reason for caution concerning this study's prediction, evaluation, interpretation, or applicability, including comparators and interpretation methods actually used; no limitations heading is required, and qualified statements count. General methodological drawbacks count when explicitly linked to their use in this study; design facts, numerical results, and future-work suggestions alone do not establish limitations or that validation was absent. Apply the existing evidence and copying rules: use supported report or supplementary wording, including study-specific checklist responses rather than checklist prompts, without supplying omitted text or translating Korean. Record contradictions about the same fact and condition separately as inconsistency, without changing status.

round1.proposed_rule: The outcome is the variable the reported models predict (e.g. the classes at a decision tree's root node). For each dataset/split on which models were developed or evaluated (including simulated datasets, labelled as such), give the proportion of each outcome class (binary: the event class). Do not code any of the following as this item: proportions of predictors; national or survey-wide figures cited as background; survey response or nonresponse rates; or missingness rates set in a simulation, unless that rate is itself the modelled outcome. If the analysis data have only an approximate statement (e.g. '95% or more' (printed in Korean)), the status is unclear. Where a % is printed for a dataset/split, use it, labelled '(weighted)' if the report says so, and add no derived duplicate. Derive a value (kind derived, formula in rationale) only for a dataset/split without a printed %, and only from printed outcome counts and n of that same dataset/split. Never derive it from PPV, NPV or other performance values, and never combine numbers from different tables or populations. Proportions within strata of the model's own score or prediction are not prevalence: if nothing else is given, the status is not_reported and the strata go in the rationale. Separate models fitted per subgroup (e.g. per sex) make each subgroup a dataset. If only subgroup proportions by participant characteristics are printed, the status is reported: give them, plus the dataset total as derived where the printed numbers allow. Cross-validation folds and bootstrap samples get no entries. For a continuous outcome the item is not_applicable, unless the report evaluates the model on categories of the outcome. In that case code the class proportions of those categories (derived from printed class counts if no % is printed). Inconsistency for this item covers only outcome proportions, their counts and their denominators: e.g. printed class counts that do not sum to the printed n of the same dataset → present. Contradictions about predictors belong to other items.

Preserve printed percentages, bounds, approximate wording and weighting: these are reported as stated, without inventing an exact point value; missing proportions for other units do not change that status. Derived proportions require matching outcome events and denominators for the same population and condition, with the formula and kind derived; do not infer prevalence from performance metrics or assume weighting, and when no eligible proportion is printed, permitted derived values leave status not_reported. Record inconsistency only for contradictory statements about the same fact, object and condition, including an explicitly exhaustive class-count total incompatible with the stated sample size; unrelated-variable discrepancies, different weighting conditions and rounding do not establish such a contradiction.

round1.proposed_rule: Count as an amount of missing data any printed number, percentage or verbal quantity (e.g. 'nearly two-thirds') of values of a study variable (outcome or predictor) that were missing or not obtained. The following are not amounts: (a) exclusions for eligibility (age, diagnosis, target population), even if the report calls them missing; (b) non-response, refusal or 'unknown' categories kept as categories of a variable, unless the report calls them missing or excludes or imputes them as missing; (c) the size of the complete-case sample, or a statement that variables are complete after incomplete rows were removed. Code 'no missing data' only when the report states that the data had none before any exclusion. (d) Missingness thresholds used as selection criteria (e.g. 'variables with >10% missing were excluded'). A printed bound without exact values (e.g. 'k features each with >20% missing') -> unclear, quoting the bound. A difference of two printed counts may be added as a derived value only when the cited text attributes the whole reduction to missing data, and on its own it never makes the status reported.

Count printed amounts explicitly describing missing, unanswered, refused or unavailable measurements, including absent or incomplete assessments and retained nonresponse categories; this does not establish how those values were handled in modelling. Count an exclusion amount only when the text links it to such unavailability or explicitly designates it as missing data; eligibility counts and procedural selection cutoffs alone do not qualify. Explicit completeness statements, verbal proportions and bounds describing observed missingness are reported for their stated scope; a calculated sample-size difference alone cannot make status reported. Keep variable, subgroup and sample-stage details within the dataset entry, without extending completeness or missingness to other scopes. Record inconsistency only for incompatible printed claims about the same fact and scope, not from assumed denominators, reconstructed totals or different exclusions.

round1.proposed_rule: The item applies whenever the report states that a threshold-based metric was computed, even if its values are in material missing from the input. It is not_applicable only when no such metric was computed. If neither method nor value is stated, the status is not_reported. A threshold is the cut-off that the report says assigns cases to outcome classes for the reported threshold-based metrics. It may be on a probability, score or single-predictor scale (e.g. 'the cut-off separating the two groups was X; accuracy Y'). Internal model parameters (tree splits not presented as the classification cut-off, latent ordinal cutpoints) and simulation data-generating values are not thresholds; quote them in the rationale only. Method means a stated criterion or procedure (default 0.5, Youden, maximise G-mean, fixed sensitivity, data used). Evaluative phrases without a criterion ('most suitable', 'optimal') give method not_reported, with the phrase quoted in the rationale. A method stated for 'all/each model' applies to every model, and value is not_reported where no number is printed for a model. When a model is evaluated at several thresholds, give one method/value pair per threshold condition, adding the condition, as the report names it, to the unit label. A more precise printed copy of the same threshold goes in the same entry (rounding only).

Use not_applicable when no threshold-based metric has a printed performance value; merely naming metrics or referencing tables does not satisfy that requirement. Otherwise, extract the classification cutoff explicitly linked to those metrics, on its stated scale: an expressly identified class-separating cutoff qualifies, while unrelated predictor, latent or simulation cutpoints alone do not. Status is reported when either the selection method or threshold number is stated, with the missing part recorded as not_reported; generic claims of suitability do not state a method, and related cutpoints alone belong in the rationale rather than making the item unclear. Apply shared methods within their expressly stated scope, retain differing model values and operating conditions with their corresponding methods, and keep two entries per evaluation without adding subgroup units or inferring datasets. Rounding is not inconsistency; record a contradiction only when supplied statements concern the same object and condition.

round1.proposed_rule: Any statement in the report about how persons or records came into the dataset counts as reported, even if no sampling design is named. Examples are 'representative sample ... sampled annually', 'derived through sampling', records taken from files that hospitals supplied, or persons randomly selected (or all survey subjects) for a measurement that defines the analysed dataset. Copy the phrase as printed (kind printed). An unnamed design or a vague procedure is not a reason for unclear or not_reported. Not_reported applies only when the report gives nothing beyond the source's name or general nature (e.g. a description of KNHANES only as a nationwide population-based survey). Give one entry per dataset. A dataset whose entry is not described gets its own entry with value 'not_reported', and the status is still reported if any dataset's entry is described.

An explicit statement that participants were sampled counts as reported, even without a named sampling design; copy the stated description without inferring further design details. round1.proposed_rule: A validation set is a dataset or held-out split on which reported performance of the model for its predicted outcome is computed. Do not list splits for which no performance is reported (e.g. used only for tuning or early stopping), or cohorts used only for a secondary analysis of another outcome. Status is reported only if n or events of at least one validation set is printed (events of the model's outcome in that set). If only split percentages or ratios, rates, or confusion-matrix cells are printed, status is not_reported. Do not enter n or events computed from them; mention them in the rationale. A confusion matrix counts as belonging to a set only if its title, legend or text says so. Record an inconsistency here only for contradictions about validation-set sizes, events, or which set or model they belong to. Contradictions in analysed-sample totals or in performance values belong to other items.

Record printed n and events for every explicitly identified validation or test set/evaluation, including separately named validation and test splits. A printed n or event count makes status reported; missing companion counts are not_reported. Partition percentages, missingness rates, whole-sample totals and confusion-matrix cells do not themselves state validation-set totals; when these alone are available, use not_reported, and do not add derived totals because this item does not authorize them. For cross-validation, record only printed fold sizes/events; exclude cross-validation used only for tuning, and include a separate analysis cohort only when the text identifies it as a prediction evaluation. Flag inconsistency only when supplied evidence establishes contradictory counts for this item's same set and condition; retain reported status for contradictory printed counts.

round1.proposed_rule: List every algorithm the report states was developed, trained, fitted or compared for the outcome. This includes statistical models, comparators and scores built from them, and models named as part of the modelling workflow. Use one entry per algorithm: unit = the name as printed, kind printed. A version the report presents as a separate model (e.g. uncalibrated, binary-output) gets its own entry. Data conditions shared by all algorithms (resampling sets, penalties) are noted inside the entries, not split. If no result is printed for a listed algorithm, add '(no results printed)'. Do not list algorithms named only as background, prior work, software capabilities, or stated as considered but not used; mention those in the rationale. Mark a model final/selected only when the report uses its own word (final, selected, chosen, proposed, primary), and quote that word. If the report only says which model performed best, record that phrase (e.g. 'highest AUC (stated)'), not 'selected'. If the report says neither, add no marker and no 'none stated' entry. Different names or abbreviation expansions for the same algorithm in the same list position (text vs table note or figure labels) are a naming difference: record the printed variant and code inconsistency none. Record inconsistency present only when one place claims to show all compared models and another place names a compared model that is missing from it.

List models explicitly stated to have been developed or compared, even without separate performance results; background mentions, software capabilities, expressly unused candidates and unlinked figure labels do not establish use. Use the permitted model units or shared study list, retaining explicitly distinguished variants and stated analytical roles without inferring additional models from components or settings. Mark final/selected only when stated; proposed, best-performing, sole-used or a finalized component does not itself establish that designation. Copy names as printed, use judged for assigned categories, and do not silently correct or equate unexplained labels. Record inconsistency only for contradictory statements about the same fact, object and condition; use uncertain when potentially conflicting statements cannot be linked to the same object, and do not treat an omitted result or additional name alone as a contradiction.

round1.proposed_rule: Code the topic of the main outcome. Count an outcome as main only if the report calls it the main or primary outcome, or calls the other outcomes secondary. If the report predicts two or more separate outcomes as equal objectives and they fall into different categories, code OTHER_OR_CROSS_CUTTING. This applies whether they are predicted by separate models or by one model predicting each disease. If they all fall into one category, code that category. Use GENERAL_HEALTH_MULTIMORBIDITY only when the outcome itself is one outcome defined as general health status, or as the coexistence or count of several conditions (multimorbidity, comorbidity, or a syndrome or phenotype defined as the coexistence of conditions from different categories). Restricting the study population to people with one condition does not change this. A composite of conditions from a single category takes that category.

round1.proposed_rule: Statistical inference means an analysis that reports p-values, significance tests, confidence intervals or adjusted effect estimates (ORs, regression coefficients). Descriptive comparisons, model performance figures and SHAP or importance plots do not count. USED: the cited statements, read together, state that the variables of an inferential analysis were chosen from ML importance or selection results. NOT_USED: the report establishes that no such link exists. Either no inferential analysis follows the ML importance or selection step, or every inferential analysis uses variables fixed independently of it (prespecified, from the literature, from significance tests run before the ML step, or all candidates). Give the order or source in the rationale; no explicit denial is needed. UNC: an inferential analysis follows the ML importance or selection step and includes variables that step selected or ranked highly, but the report does not say how its variables were chosen. NR: the report does not allow the order or the variable source of the inferential analyses to be determined. NA: the study has no ML importance or selection step.

Code USED when cited statements explicitly establish that ML importance or selection guided variable choices for subsequent statistical inference; a stated chain of decisions qualifies, even when other sources also informed the choices. Shared variables, chronology, SHAP interpretation and purely descriptive follow-up alone do not establish that link. Code NOT_USED only when non-use is stated or logically established, never from silence or an apparently complete workflow. Use NR when the link is unreported and UNC when the report addresses the link but leaves it indeterminate; NA requires that the item have no object by design. Under the legacy rules, NR and UNC still have status reported.

Statistical inference means analyses reporting p-values, significance tests, confidence intervals or adjusted effect estimates; descriptive comparisons, model performance and SHAP or importance plots do not count. round1.proposed_rule: Judge the input set of the final or reported model(s) only; candidate variables that were not retained do not count. R2 = every input is named and has a stated definition (the source question, measurement or variable, plus units for continuous inputs or categories/coding for categorical ones), and any input derived within the study (e.g. scores or model-derived features) has its computation stated. R1 = the inputs are identifiable but at least one lacks its definition, units or categories, or only some inputs are named. R0 = the input set cannot be identified (e.g. only a count, or 'selected variables'). NA = no prediction model. Names alone are R1, not R2. If two places in the report contradict each other on an input's definition or coding, that input counts as not defined (record the contradiction under inconsistency as well). Do not require KNHANES variable codes when the definition is stated in words.

Assess membership of the final predictor set(s) used in the reported prediction models; discarded candidate pools need not be recoverable. Give one study-level code: R2 when every such set is completely identifiable, R1 when some predictors are identifiable but at least one set is incomplete or ambiguous, R0 when no predictors are identifiable, and NA only when no predictor set exists by design. Use only lists or displays explicitly linked to the relevant model, without assuming that a partial display is exhaustive. Missing variable codes, measurement definitions, category boundaries, encoding, preprocessing or specifications needed to reproduce an engineered feature do not lower the code when predictor membership is fully identifiable. Assess inconsistencies separately using the existing requirement: 'present = two places in the report give contradictory information about the same fact, object and condition'; operational differences affect reconstructability only if they leave predictor membership ambiguous.

round1.proposed_rule: Judge only the inclusion and exclusion criteria (the source population and the clinical, age or design criteria). Compare them with the target population of intended use that the report states in its aim, abstract or intended-use statements. Do not count exclusions for missing or unmeasurable predictor, covariate or outcome data; they belong to the missing-data item. Do not count analysis steps applied after selection (class balancing or undersampling, outlier removal, data splitting, unweighted analysis); they belong to the analysis items. Do not count measurement limits such as a self-reported diagnosis. In each case, note the fact in the rationale. Y = all criteria are stated and every exclusion lies outside the stated target population. PY = the criteria fit the target population, but some criterion is only partly stated or its wording is ambiguous. PN = the report states an exclusion of people who belong to the stated target population (e.g. excluded for small numbers, frailty, comorbidity). N = such an exclusion is large, or the report states that the data are not representative. NI = no eligibility criteria are stated for the development data. Missing exclusion counts never make the answer NI. Use 'all models' when every model was developed on the same data.

Proposed clarification, pending verification against the official instrument and Explanation and Elaboration: Judge inclusion/exclusion against the report-stated intended-use population; do not redefine that population as the retained sample. Distinguish substantive eligibility restrictions from missing-data handling and analysis-stage sampling or preprocessing, assessing each under its designated instrument item rather than automatically treating it as a P3 failure. Use Y/N when the reported evidence clearly supports the respective conclusion, PY/PN when it supports that direction with remaining uncertainty, and NI when neither direction is supported; missing exclusion counts or retained-versus-excluded comparisons alone do not require NI or a negative answer. Apply the existing inconsistency rule separately: contradictory statements must concern the same fact, object and condition; weighted versus unweighted summaries and development versus overall counts are different objects, and an exclusion procedure alone does not establish that anyone was excluded.

round1.proposed_rule: Judge from the stated source and timing of predictor and outcome assessment; an explicit blinding statement is not required. Y = the report states predictors were assessed blind to the outcome or recorded before the outcome was determined. PY = the report names the sources of predictors and outcome (e.g. survey questionnaire, examination, laboratory) and the outcome was set by a separate measurement, test or grading, or defined afterwards by the analysts, even if blinding is not stated. PN = the report states that a predictor reflects knowledge of or a response to the outcome (e.g. a behaviour or treatment adopted because of the diagnosis); N = the report states that a predictor was assessed with outcome knowledge or built using the outcome labels. Do not infer PN or N from what a predictor might plausibly reflect. NI = the report does not state how or from what source the predictors, or the outcome, were obtained, including a derived predictor whose training labels are not stated. Give separate unit entries only for models whose values differ.

Judge how predictor values were obtained or interpreted, separately from ordinary outcome-based model fitting or predictor selection. Under PROBAST+AI, described objective assessment can support PY without explicit blinding, but this does not establish independence for unaddressed subjective predictors in the same model. Survey provenance, separate measurements, concurrent collection, predictor–outcome associations and unspecified supervised-training targets alone establish neither independence nor outcome-informed assessment. When the printed evidence supports neither direction, code NI, with status reported.

round1.proposed_rule: Derive the domain from the signalling answers: HIGH if all are Y/PY; LOW if any is N/PN; UNC if any is NI and none is N/PN. Design: answer PN/N only when the report states that the model predicts future onset or incidence and the predictors and outcome come from the same cross-sectional survey time; if the stated aim is current status, cross-sectional data is Y/PY. Selection: answer PN/N only when a stated inclusion or exclusion rule makes the data differ from the report's target population (e.g. selection that depends on the outcome or on diagnoses). Stated eligibility restrictions that match the target population and stated exclusions for missing data are PY, and rebalancing of the training set is an analysis step; neither lowers this domain. Answer NI only when the report does not state how participants were selected. Units follow the existing unit rules: one entry per final or compared model and development dataset, or 'all models' when the value is the same.

Judge source suitability, design suitability for the stated prediction task, and selection of the actual development participants separately. HIGH requires report-supported Y/PY for every applicable signalling question; LOW requires an evidence-supported critical failure—a source, design or selection feature judged N/PN because it is demonstrably or probably unsuitable for the stated task or target population; otherwise use UNC. Representative source sampling alone does not establish representativeness after selection, and eligibility restrictions, missing-data exclusions, their percentages or class balancing alone establish neither acceptable selection nor a critical failure: use NI for selection when the report does not support either judgement. Judge temporal suitability from the reported target and timing: cross-sectional status prediction is not intrinsically unsuitable, words such as 'risk' or 'incidence' alone do not establish a future target, and an explicitly future target unsupported by the reported design constitutes a design failure. For extraction, use 'all models' when the same value holds for every model and separate entries only where values differ; include only models and development datasets established by the report. Record inconsistency present only for contradictory statements about the same object and condition, uncertain when their identity cannot be resolved, and none when they concern different objects or stages.

round1.proposed_rule: Judge only how the evaluation sample was selected compared with the intended population or use stated in the report (aim, target population, setting). Code one entry per evaluation dataset (internal test, cross-validation, bootstrap, external); give no entry for development/training data alone. Exclusions made only because predictor or outcome values are missing are not judged here (they belong to the missing-data item); mention them in the rationale. The exception is missing-data handling that differs by outcome class: that is outcome-dependent selection. Y = inclusion criteria match the intended population, and every exclusion either removes persons outside it (e.g. outside the age range or the outcome definition) or is a missing-data exclusion. PY = as Y, but groups that belong to the intended population are also excluded and are small (under 10% of eligible persons by printed counts, or count not printed). PN = such groups make up 10% or more of eligible persons; or the sample comes by design from a narrower or different setting, subgroup or condition than the intended population (e.g. referral clinic, other diagnosis); or records were removed from the evaluation data by data-driven outlier filtering. N = inclusion or retention of records depends on the outcome, or the evaluation data were rebalanced or resampled (e.g. SMOTE, undersampling, case-control sampling). Outlier filtering, rebalancing and resampling count only when the report states, or cited statements establish, that they were applied to the data used for evaluation (e.g. to the whole dataset before the split). NI = the report gives no inclusion or exclusion criteria for that evaluation dataset beyond naming its source.

Proposed clarification, provisional because the official instrument and Explanation and Elaboration could not be accessed for verification: Judge the reported inclusion/exclusion process against the report’s stated intended evaluation population and setting; do not redefine that population as the retained participants. Survey representativeness, random splitting, exclusion counts, missing-data handling, clinical justification or a different outcome definition alone does not settle this item: explain how the reported selection supports or undermines representativeness, keeping missing-data and outcome/applicability judgements separate. Use Y/N when the evidence clearly establishes the direction, PY/PN when it supports that direction with uncertainty, and NI when neither direction is supported; missing information alone does not justify PN. Apply the existing rules exactly: include only supported model evaluations, group identical answers as ‘all models’, distinguish internal from external evaluation, and attribute selection, resampling or outlier removal to evaluation data only when cited statements establish that scope; record contradictions separately and only from supplied evidence about the same fact.

final_rule:
For each model | evaluation dataset (internal test, cross-validation, bootstrap or external; exclude training alone), judge selection against the report’s stated intended population and setting, with cited evidence and rationale; count outlier filtering, rebalancing or resampling only when cited statements establish that it affected evaluation data. Code N for outcome-dependent inclusion or retention, or evaluation-data rebalancing/resampling (e.g. SMOTE, undersampling, case-control sampling); otherwise PN for exclusion of intended-population groups comprising ≥10% of eligible persons by printed counts, a sample drawn by design from a narrower or different setting, subgroup or condition, or data-driven outlier removal; otherwise PY when intended-population groups are excluded but comprise <10% by printed counts or their count is not printed; otherwise Y when inclusion criteria match the intended population and exclusions remove only persons outside it.
Exception 1: Disregard exclusions solely for missing predictor or outcome values in this judgement, but describe them in the rationale; missing-data handling that differs by outcome class counts as outcome-dependent selection.
Exception 2: Code NI when no inclusion/exclusion criteria beyond the source are given, or when stated criteria and exclusion reasons do not explain the reduction from the original sample to the evaluation sample, including unreconciled stage counts; do not fill gaps with assumptions, and record contradictions separately under the general rules.

round1.proposed_rule: Judge only from data-dependent steps the report names and the data it states (or cited statements, including flow-chart order, establish) each step used; silence about households, clusters or repeated persons does not lower the response unless the report states that persons or clusters can occur in more than one split. Selecting or dropping variables by a rule that fits nothing and uses no outcome (e.g. missingness proportion, definitional removal) does not count as leakage. N: a step using the outcome or evaluation-set performance (outcome-based feature selection, tuning, threshold or outlier-threshold choice, early stopping on test loss) is stated or established to have used the evaluation data or to lie outside the folds it is evaluated with. PN: only an outcome-independent fitted step (scaling, imputation, outlier removal) used data including the evaluation data, or the order and wording place an outcome-using step before the split on 'the dataset' without restricting it to training data. Y: separate participants and every named data-dependent step fitted on training data only (within folds for cross-validation), or the evaluation data are a separate survey, cycle or country to which the model was applied without refitting and no step is stated to have been fitted on pooled development and evaluation data. PY: separate participants and at least one named step stated training-only, but the scope of another named step not stated. NI: a split is stated but nothing about the data scope of any data-dependent step.

round1.proposed_rule: Judge only from what the cited text states about the order of choices and evaluation. Only choices made from performance results count: choices that fix the reported model, its settings, its predictors or its threshold. A data-dependent step fitted on data that include the evaluation data (leakage) goes to the data-scope item and does not make this item PN. Y = the report states that every such choice was made on other data and that the model was applied to this evaluation data unchanged (without retraining, updating or recalibration). PY = the report states that settings were fixed in advance or tuned only on training data or within training-set cross-validation, and that the evaluation data were used only to evaluate. PN = the text states that such a choice was made from, or after, results on this unit's own evaluation data. N = the report says in so many words that this unit's evaluation data were used to tune or select the reported model or threshold. Reporting several compared models or configurations side by side is not by itself PN for each. NI = a choice is mentioned but the data it used are not named, or there is no information on tuning or selection. An unreported threshold counts toward NI and is never by itself PN; for evaluations that use only threshold-free metrics, judge the model and the evaluation method only.

For each model–evaluation dataset and separately evaluated model version, judge all applicable components: Y requires evidence establishing advance fixation of the model, any classification threshold used, and the evaluation method; PY requires affirmative textual support for their probable advance fixation, such as a stated development-then-evaluation sequence covering those components, rather than silence alone. Use N when cited text establishes that evaluation-data inspection informed any applicable choice, PN when linked statements support that this probably occurred, and NI when neither direction is sufficiently supported. Settings, tuning, rankings, sensitivity comparisons, an 'ad hoc' label, or validation described as occurring on training data do not alone establish such feedback or reuse of tuning folds; 'without retraining' establishes unchanged model application, and a classification threshold is relevant only to threshold-based evaluation, distinct from an outcome-defining cutoff. These are proposed extraction anchors: the official PROBAST+AI instrument and Explanation and Elaboration were unavailable for independent verification.

round2.revised_rule: Judge each unit (model or separately evaluated model version | evaluation dataset) only from what the cited text states about the data used for choices made from performance results and the order of those choices and the evaluation. Such choices are those that fix the reported model, its settings, its predictors or its classification threshold. A data-dependent step fitted on data that include the evaluation data without using performance results (e.g. univariable screening or normalisation on the whole dataset) is leakage. Code it in the data-scope item; it does not by itself make this item PN or N. An outcome-defining cutoff is not a threshold. Y = the report states that every such choice was made on other data and that the model was applied to this evaluation data unchanged (e.g. 'without retraining'). PY = the report states that settings were fixed in advance, or that model building, tuning or selection used only training data, training-set cross-validation or a separate validation split, and that this evaluation data were used only to evaluate. PN = the text states that such a choice was made from, or after, results on this unit's evaluation data (including a statement that the choice followed model validation when the only validation the report names is this unit's evaluation). N = the report states in so many words that this unit's evaluation data were used to fit, tune or select the reported model or threshold (e.g. performance reported on the same training set on which tuning was done). Reporting compared models or configurations side by side, naming the best of them, or sensitivity comparisons is not by itself PN. NI = settings are only listed, a choice is mentioned without naming the data it used, or there is no information on tuning or selection. An unreported threshold counts toward NI and is never by itself PN; for evaluations that use only threshold-free metrics, judge the model and the evaluation method only.

For each model–evaluation dataset and separately evaluated version, judge whether the model, any classification threshold used, and the evaluation method were fixed before inspecting that evaluation data. Use N when cited statements establish that any applicable component was not fixed beforehand, PN when linked statements affirmatively support this as probable. Otherwise use Y when advance fixation of every applicable component is established, PY when affirmative text supports it as probable, and NI when neither direction is sufficiently supported. A stated development-then-evaluation sequence can support PY when it covers the applicable components. Missing information does not override evidence for N or PN. A classification threshold matters only for threshold-based evaluation and is distinct from an outcome-defining cutoff. Settings, unspecified tuning, rankings, sensitivity comparisons, an 'ad hoc' label, and evaluation on training data do not alone establish the required timing or reuse of tuning folds. round1.proposed_rule: Derive PE_D1 from PE_P1–P3 only: LOW if all are Y/PY, HIGH if any is N/PN, otherwise UNC. P1/P2: a national survey is an appropriate source; a cross-sectional design is appropriate for a model of current (prevalent or diagnostic) status and is PN only when the report states that the model predicts future onset. P3: judge the stated selection of the evaluation sample against the population the report states the model is for. Answer PY when the sample is the persons meeting the stated inclusion criteria (e.g. age band, completed examination, condition of interest). Answer PN when the report states a selection that narrows or skews the sample relative to that population (e.g. a sample recruited only from a subgroup of it, an exclusion of a clinical subgroup of the eligible population, or the report's own statement that excluded persons differ or that selection cannot be characterised). Answer NI when the report gives no criteria for how the analysed records were selected. Exclusions for missing values or outliers (complete case) are judged in the analysis domain, not here, unless the report states that the excluded persons differ from the included. Judge each evaluation dataset (internal test, cross-validation, external) separately; development/apparent results are not units.

Judge data-source, design and participant-selection appropriateness against the report's stated target population and evaluated outcome and timing. A national survey label does not establish the appropriateness of its analysed subset; clinic recruitment, eligibility restrictions, complete-case exclusions or exclusion counts alone do not establish bias. Do not infer future prediction from the word 'risk': cross-sectional data can support concurrent classification, but cannot establish future outcome occurrence. For each signalling question, assign Y/PY when cited text supports appropriateness, N/PN when it supports a material participant/data-source failure likely to bias that evaluation, and NI when appropriateness cannot be determined; code HIGH if any such N/PN establishes a critical failure, LOW if all responses are Y/PY, and UNC otherwise. Apply a concern only to evaluations using the affected data. Following the existing rules, give one entry per model–evaluation dataset the report distinguishes, using 'all models' when the same value applies; do not infer an evaluation from development data or extend a procedure to another model without a stated link, and never classify a held-out split of the same data as external.

round1.proposed_rule: C10 is met only when the report itself explicitly addresses the outcome-predictor overlap: it states that the variables defining the outcome (or the items or components of the outcome measure) were left out of the predictors, or were kept as predictors, and says how this was handled or why (a stated reason is enough). If you could only tell whether there was overlap by comparing the outcome definition with the predictor list, the criterion is not_met. This applies whether the comparison would show no overlap or shows the defining variables kept as predictors. Separating the dependent variable from the independent variables in a table, or listing defining variables among the retained predictors, is not such a statement. Status is reported for both met and not_met; it is not_applicable only when the study has no outcome definition built from variables that could also be predictors.

Code met when the reported outcome definition and identified model inputs establish whether outcome-defining variables were used and their disposition, including retention, transformation, or nonuse; no separate overlap discussion, justification, or corrective action is required. An explicitly complete final input list can establish nonuse in that model, but does not establish deliberate removal or absence from an earlier candidate pool. Count only variables identified by the report as defining the outcome, not merely related constructs; list completeness and variable identity must be established by the supplied text, not assumed from headings or isolated cells. If this cannot be established, code not_met; use not_applicable only when the criterion has no object.

round1.proposed_rule: Code only the outcome(s) that the report states a prediction model was fitted (trained) to predict for the study's stated aim. Do not count outcomes of auxiliary models that serve that aim (e.g. models that form strata or weights, propensity models, imputation of predictors). Do not count endpoints a fitted model is only evaluated against: further or external labels, subgroup discriminations, or outcomes of a comparator or existing score. Mention these in the rationale. MULTIBIN applies only when the report states that separate models were fitted for two or more different binary outcomes. MIXED applies only when fitted outcomes differ in type (e.g. binary and continuous). If the outcome definition or model specification (classes, output layer, loss) states one structure and the results show another for the same model, code the structure stated in the outcome definition or model specification, and record inconsistency present citing both places.

Classify all distinct targets explicitly predicted or discriminated by the study’s evaluated prediction models, including secondary analyses, validation-only targets, comparators and other datasets; separate training for each target is not required. Count the same target once across models, datasets and subgroups; exclude subgroup labels and variables used only for imputation or preprocessing. Use BINARY for one binary target, MULTIBIN for several distinct binary targets, and MIXED for explicitly modelled targets of different structures; neither a different endpoint name nor binary-sounding performance metrics alone establish an additional binary task. Apply the existing contradiction rules: retain conflicting supported codes in the single study-level entry, separated by '; ', with status reported and inconsistency present, citing both statements; do not resolve the contradiction by choosing one description or coding MIXED.

round1.proposed_rule: Count as fitted algorithms only the prediction-model families the authors trained. Versions of one family (different inputs, settings or architectures, or a baseline with fewer inputs) count as one family. Regressions used only for association or confounder adjustment, and published scores the authors did not fit, are not counted. If only one family remains, code single_algorithm. A model is designated when the text calls it final, chosen, proposed or recommended. It is also designated when the text says it had the best or higher performance overall compared with all other fitted families, or when the authors say they favour it. Do not designate from table values alone, and do not designate because a model received explanation analyses (e.g. SHAP). If the stated lead holds only for some metrics, subgroups or competitors and no overall choice is stated, code Not designated. Inconsistency for this item concerns only which model is designated or best (e.g. the text names one model best while the cited table gives that value to another model). Record the authors' designation as the value.

Count distinct algorithms stated to have been fitted for prediction; exclude methods used only for association or adjustment, and do not count different inputs, settings or subgroup fits as additional algorithms. If only one prediction algorithm was fitted, code single_algorithm even when a variant is called best. Otherwise, code the family of a model the authors unambiguously designate as final, preferred or best overall; an unambiguous contextual reference suffices, but metric-specific rankings, favorable discussion and interpretive analyses alone do not, and without a study-level designation code Not designated. Apply the existing inconsistency rule to this item's fact—the author designation or selected family—so discrepancies confined to predictor counts or performance do not establish inconsistency here.

round1.proposed_rule: REP15 components: (1) participant flow is reported when the report prints the number of participants at two or more stages, at least a starting or eligible count and the analysed count, in text or a flow diagram. (2) Exclusions are reported when the report states the exclusion or selection criteria (reasons) that led to the analysed sample. Counts per reason are not required. Do not assume exclusions the report does not state. (3) Analysed participant characteristics are reported when descriptive values (e.g. mean/SD, n/%) of participant variables other than the outcome are printed for the analysed sample, overall or by group. round1.proposed_rule: The two components are judged for the study as a whole. 'Performance estimate' means at least one named metric with a printed value for a model. A bound or a summary that names no metric (e.g. 'above 90% in all aspects') is not an estimate. 'Uncertainty' means any printed CI, SD, SE, ± value, IQR or range attached to a model's performance estimate, or printed per-fold or bootstrap values or a histogram of them. This counts even if it is given for only some models or datasets (e.g. only cross-validation results) or its meaning is not defined; say which estimates it covers and what is undefined in the rationale. Uncertainty given only for differences between models, or p-values and test statistics, is not uncertainty of a performance estimate. R = both components printed; P = estimates printed with no uncertainty for any model's estimate; NR = no estimate printed. Inconsistency is present when the same model, dataset and metric are printed with different estimates or CIs in two places (beyond rounding), or when a point estimate lies outside its own printed interval. It is uncertain when one of the places does not name the model, metric or dataset. It is none when equal or different numbers belong to different statistics or models.

Count an explicitly stated numerical predictive-performance result or bound even when its metric is unnamed; leave the metric unspecified. At study level, R requires at least one performance estimate with a reported interval, ± quantity or explicitly identified resampling distribution; uncertainty need not cover every model, metric or dataset, and an unspecified ± type must remain unspecified. Uncertainty for between-model differences does not supply uncertainty for individual performance estimates; separate runs or a statement that resampling occurred do not alone establish a resampling distribution. Use P when only one required component is reported and NR when neither is reported; put only the code in the value and list reported components in the rationale. Apply inconsistency separately: require conflicting printed statements about the same fact, object and condition, use uncertain when their identity is unresolved, and never change reporting completeness because of inconsistency; implausibility or a point estimate outside its interval alone does not meet that definition.

round1.proposed_rule: Count each component only when the report text (including abstract and highlights) explicitly states it. Limitations: a statement naming a weakness of this study's design, data, measurement, methods or results. Future-work plans count only when they name such a weakness. Generalisability: a statement about whether the results or model apply to people, settings or data beyond the study sample. This includes stated restrictions (e.g. one country only, no survey weights, sample limited to a group 'may restrict generalisability') and calls to test the results in other populations or data. A sample description, an excluded subgroup, a 'representative data' strength claim or 'the method could be used for other diseases' counts only if the report ties it to whether the results transfer. Applicability: a statement of how, by whom or in which practical setting or decision the model or its findings would be used (e.g. screening, clinical decision support, targeting interventions, policy or health programmes). Statements about the disease's importance, the method's performance or future research alone do not count. Code R if all three are stated, P if one or two, NR if none, and list the stated components in the rationale with their IDs.

Count only components explicitly stated in the report or supplements: limitations name a weakness of this study’s design, data, measurement, methods or results (future-work plans count only when they identify such a weakness); generalisability discusses whether the findings or model apply beyond the study sample, including calls for testing in other populations or datasets; applicability states how, by whom, or in which practical setting or decision the model or findings would be used, beyond statements of the prediction task, performance, disease importance or future research alone. Record only R for all three components, P for one or two, or NR for none, and list the supported components with evidence IDs in the rationale.

Count representativeness as generalisability only when the report presents it as a strength or limitation supporting which population the findings apply to; sample descriptions or exclusions alone do not count.

round1.proposed_rule:
Judge PD_A2 from what the report prints about the data each model was developed on.
(1) Y only when the report gives a sample-size calculation or a learning curve showing the sample is adequate. N when the report says the sample is inadequate.
(2) Otherwise compute EPV = participants in the smaller outcome class in the development data / number of candidate predictors (all variables considered before any selection). Give it as a derived value in the rationale, with the formula. Grades: EPV >=20 -> PY; 10 to <20 -> PN; <10 -> N. Use the same cut-offs for every model family. Unreported model complexity or hyperparameters do not change the grade.

(5) Give one entry per final or compared model and development dataset. Group models as 'all models | <dataset>' when the answer is the same.

round1.proposed_rule: Judge each evaluation dataset only by its numbers of participants with and without the outcome (for multiclass outcomes, every class). For cross-validation or bootstrap, use all the data evaluated across the folds. For an internal test, use the held-out set. Count real participants only; oversampled or synthetic records do not count. Y = a precision-based sample-size justification is stated, or counts printed for that dataset (or summed from its printed cells, such as confusion-matrix rows) give at least 100 in every outcome class. N = such counts give fewer than 100 in any class. PY or PN = the same 100 cut-off, but the counts are only estimated by multiplying printed totals or prevalence by the printed split fraction (give the formula in the rationale). NI = neither printed nor estimable counts exist. Missing CIs, no sample-size calculation, and authors' general remarks without numbers do not change the answer; mention them in the rationale. If places in the report give contradictory counts, answer from them when every reading leads to the same response, otherwise NI.

Count distinct evaluated participants without treating folds, repeated splits or synthetic observations as additional independent participants, and do not assume pooled cross-validation performance when only fold-averaged results are stated.
