round1.proposed_rule: Resampling evaluation = cross-validation, bootstrap, or a random split repeated with refitting, whose results are reported as performance; a single split, a temporal hold-out, an external evaluation, and cross-validation used only for tuning are not resampling. If no reported evaluation uses resampling, status not_applicable with no entries; otherwise give each resampling evaluation a code and each non-resampling evaluation NA. Y = every data-dependent step is stated as done inside each resample. PY = the report states that fitting or the whole analysis was repeated in each resample, and every other data-dependent step it names is either stated as inside the resamples or fixed in advance without using the data. N = a named data-dependent step (tuning, predictor or algorithm selection, imputation, scaling, class-imbalance resampling, outlier removal) is stated as done once outside the resamples, or within the same resamples whose results are reported without nesting; PN = the stated order of steps only implies this. NI = the report does not state what was repeated.

Proposed clarification; the official instrument and Explanation and Elaboration could not be independently verified. Assess each reported model evaluation separately: as an exception to the general validation-applicability rule, use NA for an identified holdout or frozen external evaluation without resampling evaluation, and NI when the evaluation’s relationship to resampling cannot be determined. Cross-validation confined to tuning, unspecified repetitions and bootstrap confidence intervals alone do not establish resampling evaluation; do not invent additional evaluation datasets or repeated splits. For resampling evaluation, assess repetition within each training resample of all applicable data-dependent development steps, including learned preprocessing, selection and tuning; deliberately fixed components require no redevelopment, including a frozen base model when evaluating newly fitted recalibration. Use Y or N when repetition of all applicable steps, or failure to repeat at least one, is established; use PY or PN when cited evidence supports that direction without establishing it, and NI when the direction remains unresolved. Silence, procedural order, an ‘optimal model’, or evidence about only some steps does not by itself establish either direction; retain the existing legacy response-code, status and unit conventions.

If no reported evaluation uses resampling, status not_applicable with no entries; otherwise give each resampling evaluation a code and each other evaluation NA. If the report states that an evaluation was repeated but not whether the model was refitted in each run, code that evaluation NI. PY = the report states that the fitting, the analysis or the experiment was repeated in each resample (naming k-fold cross-validation or bootstrap validation counts), and every other data-dependent step it names is either stated as inside the resamples or was fixed before the evaluation data were used (e.g. predictors taken from the literature, preset hyperparameters, a frozen base model being recalibrated). round1.proposed_rule: USED = a stated step that uses the outcome to choose or drop the inputs of a prediction model whose performance is reported, before that model is fitted or refitted. Examples: univariable or significance screening; a correlation filter that keeps the variable more strongly associated with the outcome; LASSO, RFE or stepwise selection; refitting on an importance-ranked subset. None of the following counts as USED by itself: variable choice inside the algorithm (tree splitting, regularisation penalties); importance rankings or top-k lists made after fitting, with no model refitted on the reduced set; selection that feeds only a secondary association, sensitivity or interpretive analysis not evaluated as a prediction model (mention it in the rationale). NOT_USED = the cited statements establish that the model inputs were fixed without using the outcome (literature-based or prespecified sets, missing-data or other unsupervised filters) and entered into the model as they were. NR = the report does not say how the model inputs were obtained. UNC = an outcome-based 'selection' is described but the text does not fix whether it restricted the inputs of the evaluated model.

Code USED when the report states that an outcome-dependent procedure selected, retained or removed predictors for a prediction model, including a prediction comparator; selection solely for association estimation or interpretation does not count. Ordinary tree splitting and importance rankings or top-variable displays alone do not count, but using such rankings to choose predictors for prediction-model fitting does. At study level, USED requires at least one qualifying use; NOT_USED requires stated nonuse or statements logically establishing its absence across the prediction models, rather than literature-based inclusion, unsupervised filtering or silence alone. Otherwise use NR when qualifying selection is unreported, or UNC when the text describes possible qualifying selection but its nature or application cannot be determined. Assess inconsistency only from supplied, in-scope evidence: present requires contradictory statements about the same fact, object and condition; uncertain requires a possible contradiction whose objects cannot be distinguished; none applies when no contradiction is found.

round1.proposed_rule: Code the tuning step and the model-selection step together. NOT_USED: the cited text says the final, best or optimal model, its feature subset or its settings were chosen by comparing results on the same data (test set, validation set or cross-validation folds) whose results are reported as the final performance. This includes reporting only the best result over a grid or feature subsets when no separate tuning data are stated, and it applies even when tuning itself stayed within the training data. USED: tuning, and any choice of model, is stated to use only training data or inner resampling, apart from the data of the reported estimates. NA: the report states fixed, preset or default settings with no search and no data-driven choice among models, or the study has no test, validation or resampled evaluation data at all. NR: tuning or selection is described, but the report doesn't state which data it used. Don't infer which data a selection used: count it only when the text, a table or figure title, or a note names those data.

Code USED when the report establishes that tuning and any reported model selection were confined to training data or inner resampling; code NOT_USED when cited statements establish that final-evaluation data or their results were used for either decision; otherwise code NR. A statement explicitly selecting the final model using the reported evaluation results establishes reuse even without a named split; merely comparing models, calling one best, matching performance numbers, or omitting nested-resampling details does not. Code NA only when absence of tuning and model selection is stated or logically established, never merely from listed settings or silence. Under the legacy status rule, USED, NOT_USED and NR have status reported; NA has status not_applicable.

round2.revised_rule: Code tuning and model selection together. NA (status not_applicable): the study has no test, validation or resampled evaluation data at all, or the report states that settings were fixed, preset or default (no search) and no model is chosen from results. NOT_USED: the text states that the final or best model, its settings or its feature subset was chosen from the reported evaluation results, or that only the best result over a grid or over feature subsets is reported with no separate tuning data stated, or a text, title or note names the final-evaluation data as the data of the selection comparison. This applies even if tuning itself stayed within training data. Comparing models that are all reported, or calling one best or optimal, is not a selection. USED: tuning is stated to use only training data or inner resampling, and any described selection is stated to do the same. NR: any other case, including a tuning or selection step whose data are not stated. Do not infer the data from matching numbers or from a flowchart step.

round1.proposed_rule: Judge this item mainly on the printed handling of continuous predictors (kept continuous, transformed, or categorised and at which cut points), and secondarily on how categorical predictors were coded or grouped. Y = continuous predictors are stated as kept continuous or transformed with a graded transform (scaling, standardisation, splines, overlapping fuzzy membership functions), and the coding of categorical predictors is stated and keeps their categories distinct. PY = continuous handling is stated as above, but categorical encoding is not described; a missing dummy or one-hot description alone never gives NI. Merging the levels of a predictor that was already categorical or ordinal into broader groups also gives PY. PN = any continuous predictor was dichotomised or categorised at a cut point set from the study's own data (the sample mean, median, quantiles, or an optimal or tree-derived cut point), or a nominal predictor with more than two categories is printed as entered as a numeric or standardised continuous value. Categorisation at a stated conventional or pre-specified cut point gives PY. NI = the report does not state how the continuous predictors were entered. Recoding of missing, 'unknown' or 'not applicable' answers belongs to the missing-data item, not this one. Put the printed basis for the rating in the rationale.

Proposed operational clarification; the official instrument and Explanation and Elaboration could not be independently verified here: Use Y/PY when reported handling supports an appropriate judgement for all predictor types used; use NI when essential handling information is missing, and N/PN when reported handling establishes or suggests a material defect. Variable-type labels, descriptive summaries, interface controls, scaling and silence about categorisation are insufficient alone, whereas an explicit statement that numeric codes were used solely as category labels can support PY without software-level confirmation. Scaling/PCA, graded fuzzy membership, tree-learned splits and regrouping existing categories are not automatically inappropriate; unjustified pre-model dichotomisation of continuous inputs or merging unknown responses with a substantive category supports PN, accounting for stated exclusions without assuming unreported category meanings or retained unknown observations. Apply the existing rules literally: code every compared model–development dataset, use evidence only for the handling and units it explicitly describes, distinguish display transformations from model preprocessing, and assess contradictions separately using the same-object-and-condition test.

round2.revised_rule: Judge mainly how continuous predictors entered the model and secondarily how categorical predictors were coded or grouped. Continuous handling counts as stated only when the report describes the model inputs or their preprocessing. Examples: variables listed as continuous model inputs, scaled/standardised/normalised, imputed and entered as numbers, per-unit coefficients, or graded transforms (splines, fuzzy membership functions). Descriptive summaries (mean/SD in a characteristics table), user-interface controls and values shown in explanation plots do not show how a predictor entered the model. Y = continuous handling stated as kept continuous or graded-transformed, and categorical coding stated in a way that keeps categories distinct (dummy/one-hot, declared categorical). PY = continuous handling stated, but categorical coding is not described, or is described only as numeric codes meant as labels without saying how the model treated them. Merging levels of an already categorical or ordinal predictor, or categorising at a stated conventional or pre-specified cut point, also gives PY. A missing encoding description alone never gives NI. PN = before entering the model, a continuous predictor was dichotomised or categorised at a cut point taken from the study's own data (sample mean, median, quantiles, optimal or separately tree-derived cut point). PN also applies when a predictor with more than two unordered categories (shown by its printed categories or name, e.g. occupation, marital status) is printed as z-scored, standardised or entered as a continuous number. Splits learned by a tree model itself are not categorisation. Ordered categories (e.g. a Likert scale) entered as scores are not a defect, even if the report labels them 'nominal'. NI = the report does not state how the continuous predictors entered the model. Recoding of missing, 'unknown' or 'not applicable' answers belongs to the missing-data item. Put the printed basis in the rationale.

round3_candidates.P: Judge mainly how continuous predictors entered the model and secondarily how categorical predictors were coded or grouped. Continuous handling counts as stated only when the report describes the model inputs or their preprocessing. Examples: variables listed as continuous model inputs, scaled/standardised/normalised, imputed and entered as numbers, per-unit coefficients, or graded transforms (splines, fuzzy membership functions). Descriptive summaries (mean/SD in a characteristics table), user-interface controls and values shown in explanation plots do not show how a predictor entered the model. Y = continuous handling stated as kept continuous or graded-transformed, and categorical coding stated in a way that keeps categories distinct (dummy/one-hot, declared categorical). PY = continuous handling stated, but categorical coding is not described, or is described only as numeric codes meant as labels without saying how the model treated them. Merging levels of an already categorical or ordinal predictor, or categorising at a stated conventional or pre-specified cut point, also gives PY. A missing encoding description alone never gives NI. PN = before entering the model, a continuous predictor was dichotomised or categorised at a cut point taken from the study's own data (sample mean, median, quantiles, optimal or separately tree-derived cut point). PN also applies when a predictor with more than two unordered categories (shown by its printed categories or name, e.g. occupation, marital status) is printed as z-scored, standardised or entered as a continuous number. Splits learned by a tree model itself are not categorisation. Ordered categories (e.g. a Likert scale) entered as scores are not a defect, even if the report labels them 'nominal'. NI = the report does not state how the continuous predictors entered the model. Recoding of missing, 'unknown' or 'not applicable' answers belongs to the missing-data item. Put the printed basis in the rationale.
round3_candidates.Q: Proposed operational clarification; the official instrument and Explanation and Elaboration could not be independently verified here: Use Y/PY when reported handling supports an appropriate judgement for all predictor types used; use NI when essential handling information is missing, and N/PN when reported handling establishes or suggests a material defect. Variable-type labels, descriptive summaries, interface controls, scaling and silence about categorisation are insufficient alone, whereas an explicit statement that numeric codes were used solely as category labels can support PY without software-level confirmation. Scaling/PCA, graded fuzzy membership, tree-learned splits and regrouping existing categories are not automatically inappropriate; unjustified pre-model dichotomisation of continuous inputs or merging unknown responses with a substantive category supports PN, accounting for stated exclusions without assuming unreported category meanings or retained unknown observations. Apply the existing rules literally: code every compared model–development dataset, use evidence only for the handling and units it explicitly describes, distinguish display transformations from model preprocessing, and assess contradictions separately using the same-object-and-condition test.

rule_source: no agreement; suggested rule adopted under the author's direction
final_rule:
Code Y when continuous predictors are explicitly retained as numeric inputs or given graded transformations and categorical predictors are explicitly treated as categorical; code PY when continuous handling is stated but categorical coding is missing or uncertain, existing categories are regrouped, or continuous predictors are categorised at explicitly conventional or prespecified cut points; code NI when handling of continuous predictors used cannot be established. Base these judgements on stated model inputs or preprocessing, not descriptive summaries, interface controls or explanation displays; ordered-category scores and splits learned within trees are not defects, and recoding missing, unknown or not-applicable responses belongs to the missing-data item.

- Code PN for pre-model categorisation of continuous predictors using study-derived cut points or cut points not explicitly described as conventional or prespecified, including an unstated source.
- Code PN when the report states that an unordered predictor with more than two categories was entered as a single numeric input, including label encoding or standardisation.

round1.proposed_rule: Use NI only when the report and its supplement state nothing about missing data or how it was handled. Once a handling method is stated, judge from that method; missing details (amount of missingness, imputation settings, number of imputed sets, timing relative to the split) go in the rationale and never produce NI. Multiple imputation, or model-based imputation of predictors (MICE/PMM, iterative, KNN), counts as PY; it counts as Y only when the report also prints the amount of missing data and states that the outcome was used in the imputation model, or that no data were missing. Single simple imputation (mean, median, mode, or 'simple imputation') counts as PN. Excluding participants with missing predictor data (complete-case) counts as PN when the number excluded for missingness is not printed, and as N when printed counts show the loss. Excluding participants only because their outcome is missing does not by itself change the rating. When the imputer was fitted relative to the split is coded in the data-scope (leakage) item, not here. When the outcome is not time-to-event, censoring does not apply; judge on missing data alone and say so in the rationale. Code the final model and every model the report evaluates equally, and give one 'all models | <development dataset>' entry when the response is the same for all of them.

For each reported final or compared model–development-dataset, assess the stated handling of missing predictors, missing outcomes and relevant censoring using the official PROBAST+AI guidance: Y/N require support for a definite judgement, PY/PN require support for a probable directional judgement, and NI applies when neither direction is supportable. Neither naming an imputation method nor omitting reporting details alone determines the response; assess the reported context without an automatic method hierarchy or an invented missingness cutoff. Code only what the report and its supplementary material state; never fill from general knowledge or from what is usual for KNHANES. No unsupported inference: never enter a number, procedure, split or timing that the report does not state.

final_rule:

round1.proposed_rule: Derive the judgement per unit from that unit's analysis signalling responses only: HIGH if all are Y/PY; LOW if any is N/PN (critical failure); otherwise UNC (at least one NI, none N/PN). Assign each response from printed text: an absent statement or justification is NI, never PN. A1 is N when the only performance printed for the model is on the data it was fitted on. A2: Y/PY when a stated sample-size calculation is met or when EPV (printed, or derived from printed event and candidate-predictor counts) is >=20; PN when EPV <10; NI when EPV is 10-<20 or the counts are not printed. A3 is PN when continuous predictors are stated to be categorised or dichotomised. A4 is PN when participants with missing or incomplete data are stated to be excluded, PY when imputation is stated, and NI when the report is silent. A5 is PN when a data-driven selection, tuning or model-choice step is stated to have used the evaluation data, and NI when its data scope is not stated. A step shared by several models gives them the same response; use 'all models' when every unit gets the same value. Leave inconsistency as none unless the conflict concerns a fact used for these responses.

For this item, define a critical failure as at least one analysis signalling response of N or PN: assign LOW if any applicable response is N/PN, HIGH if every applicable response is Y/PY, and UNC otherwise; assign NA only when no model-development object exists. Establish each signalling response from cited report statements: insufficient information is NI, and neither missing detail nor a method name alone establishes appropriateness or failure. Unstated procedural scope remains unstated, and stated validation must be considered even when only apparent results are printed. Apply the judgement separately to each model–development dataset, combining entries only when the same judgement and supporting responses apply.

round2.revised_rule: Judge each unit ('model | development dataset') from its analysis signalling responses only: LOW if any is N/PN (critical failure); HIGH if all are Y/PY; otherwise UNC. A step shared by several models gives them all the same response; use 'all models' when every unit gets the same value. A1 (evaluation): Y when performance is printed on held-out, cross-validation, bootstrap or external data; N when the only performance printed for the model is on the data it was fitted on, or when no evaluation data are stated. A2 (sample size): Y/PY when a stated sample-size calculation is met, or when events per candidate predictor (printed, or derived from printed counts) is 20 or more; PN when it is below 10; NI when it is 10 to below 20 or the counts are not printed. A3 (predictors): PN when any continuous predictor is stated to be categorised or dichotomised; Y/PY when continuous predictors are stated to be kept continuous (including scaled) and none is stated to be categorised; else NI. A4 (missing data): PN when participants with missing or incomplete data are stated to be excluded, even if imputation is also stated; PY when only imputation is stated; NI when the report is silent. A5 (overfitting/data scope): PN when a data-driven selection, tuning or model-choice step is stated to have used the evaluation data; NI when the data scope of any such step is not stated; Y/PY when every such step is stated to use only training data or folds, or settings are stated to be fixed in advance. Record inconsistency only for conflicting facts that these responses rest on.

final_rule: For each ‘model | development dataset’, assign LOW if any applicable analysis signalling response is N/PN, HIGH if all are Y/PY, and UNC otherwise; assign NA only when no model-development object exists, apply shared steps to every affected model, and use ‘all models | development dataset’ when the responses and judgement are the same. round1.proposed_rule: Code each model x evaluation dataset only from the performance measures printed for that dataset. A number counts only if the text, table or figure labels it as that measure and links it to that dataset. Discrimination means AUROC, PR-AUC or C-statistic; for a continuous target it means an error or fit measure (RMSE, MAE, R2). Calibration means a calibration plot, calibration slope or intercept, O/E ratio or calibration test; for a continuous target it means an observed-vs-predicted plot or a mean bias. Codes: Y = discrimination and calibration both printed. PY = discrimination printed, and calibration only stated in words without any plot or value. PN = discrimination printed, no calibration (with or without threshold measures or net benefit). N = no discrimination measure printed for that evaluation, only accuracy, threshold-based measures or a misclassification/risk estimate. NI = no performance measure printed for that evaluation. Do not change the code for missing uncertainty, inconsistencies, test-set balancing, the comparison test, multiclass averaging or class weighting; record these in their own items or in the rationale.

Proposed operational addition, requiring verification against the official PROBAST+AI Explanation and Elaboration, which was unavailable here: judge adequacy for the explicitly stated target, output and intended use—predicted risks require discrimination and calibration, hard-class predictions require suitable class-specific assessment, and continuous reconstruction may be adequately assessed with task-aligned error measures; do not infer the output type from the algorithm or a tool’s name. Require threshold performance or net benefit when necessary to substantiate the stated decision-use claim, and do not make absent net benefit or confidence intervals an automatic failure for every task. Use Y or N when the evidence establishes appropriate or inappropriate assessment, PY or PN when it supports that conclusion only probably, and NI when neither direction is supported; an unreported assessment does not establish that it was not performed, and a documented flaw must affect the coded evaluation to justify downgrading it. Apply the existing extraction rules: code each distinguished model evaluation, combine units only when the same judgement applies, add no unsupported subgroup units or procedures, count metrics only when values are printed, and record contradictions separately using the same-object-and-condition requirement.

A goodness-of-fit test alone (e.g. Hosmer–Lemeshow) is not calibration. Codes: Y = discrimination and calibration both printed. PY = discrimination printed, and calibration only stated in words without any plot or value. PN = discrimination printed, no calibration (with or without threshold measures or net benefit). Do not change the code for missing uncertainty, inconsistencies, test-set balancing, the comparison test, multiclass averaging or class weighting; record these in their own items or in the rationale.

For each model | evaluation dataset, judge whether the reported measures and their calculation appropriately assess the explicitly stated target, output and intended use. Predicted probabilities require discrimination and calibration; explicitly established hard-class-only outputs require suitable assessment of relevant classes and errors; continuous prediction or reconstruction may be adequately assessed with task-appropriate error or fit measures. Do not infer output type from an algorithm, score or tool name, or infer that reporting classification measures establishes the absence of probability outputs. Require threshold performance or net benefit when needed to substantiate an explicit decision-use claim, not universally. Use Y or N when evidence clearly establishes adequate or inadequate assessment, PY or PN when it supports that conclusion only probably, and NI when neither direction is supported, including when missing task or output information prevents judgement. An unreported assessment does not establish that it was not performed; explain why any missing assessment supports a probable judgement. Missing confidence intervals or a contradiction is not an automatic downgrade; a documented flaw must affect assessment of the coded evaluation. Apply the existing rules for evaluation units, printed metric values, evidence, legacy status and separate recording of inconsistencies.

final_rule: For each model | evaluation dataset, use only performance evidence explicitly identified and linked to that evaluation: discrimination means AUROC, PR-AUC or C-statistic, or error/fit measures for continuous targets; calibration means a calibration plot, slope, intercept or O/E ratio, or an observed-versus-predicted plot or mean bias for continuous targets, and a goodness-of-fit test alone does not qualify. round1.proposed_rule: Important variables are the variables that the report's text names as most important, top-ranked or as the largest contributors, based on a result of the prediction model. Such results include feature or permutation importance, SHAP, the model's coefficients or scores, and the first or main splits of a tree when the text says so. Only when the text names none, use the variables of a table or figure whose title designates them as top or important. Never code a full printed ranking beyond what is so designated. Never code a variable only because it appears among the predictors, the definitions or the descriptive results. If the report designates no important variable, code NA (not_applicable). Map each designated variable to the domain of what it measures. Body composition (fat, muscle, water, circumferences) goes under ADIPOSITY_BODY_SIZE. A diagnosis or treatment of the person goes under the domain of that condition when one exists (diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidaemia, depression, musculoskeletal); otherwise, and for family history, occupation and medication use, it goes under WORK_CLINICAL_HISTORY. Laboratory values, reproductive factors and senses with no domain go under OTHER, described in the rationale. List each domain once.

Use the variables explicitly highlighted by the authors as important or leading contributors, including additional contributors explicitly highlighted elsewhere; only when no highlighted subset is stated, use the complete displayed global importance ranking, without inventing a cutoff. As the existing rules require, accept stated predictive influence regardless of the method, including explicitly influential tree splits and ranked model-score contributions; candidate lists and variable definitions alone do not establish importance, and missing importance information does not establish absence by design. Map each selected variable by its specific measured content rather than its framing as history or a reason for activity restriction: body-composition measures, including water and lean mass, belong to ADIPOSITY_BODY_SIZE, and disease-specific personal or family history belongs to the corresponding disease domain. Reserve WORK_CLINICAL_HISTORY for work or clinical history without a more specific listed domain; use OTHER for content outside the listed domains and describe it in the rationale. Use only report-defined variable meanings, and return each domain code once at study level.

final_rule:
Code each domain once at study level from the union of variables the text identifies as important, top, influential or ranked by importance in prediction-model results and variables in tables or figures the authors designate as top or important; if no subset is designated, use the complete displayed global importance ranking without a cutoff. Exception: If the report contains no importance results, code NA.

round1.proposed_rule: Feature selection here means a data-driven step that chooses which inputs enter a model the study fits, including a later model (e.g. univariable significance filters, importance-ranked top variables passed to a regression, LASSO or wrapper selection). It is not the variables a fitted tree chooses for its own splits (e.g. CHAID chi-square node splitting), predictors fixed in advance from the literature or a theory, entering all listed variables, or importance only reported after fitting. When no such step is described, code NA (status not_applicable). When a selection step exists: code WITHIN, TRAIN or BEFORE only if cited statements tie the step to the data it used relative to the stated split or resampling. If cited statements show the step used the whole analysed sample and the report describes no split or resampling, code OTHER (rationale: 'selection on the whole analysed sample; no split described'). Otherwise code ORDER_NR.

Active feature selection means a reported data-dependent choice of the input predictor set used to construct an evaluated prediction model, including an embedded procedure explicitly described as making that choice. Prior candidate choice, ordinary tree-node splitting, importance reporting, and selection solely for a subsequent explanatory analysis do not by themselves establish such an intervention or its absence; using every listed predictor also does not establish that no earlier selection occurred. Use NA only when the report states or logically establishes that no qualifying intervention occurred; otherwise use ORDER_NR when the intervention or its timing cannot be established. Assign WITHIN, TRAIN, BEFORE or OTHER only from statements linking the qualifying selection to the relevant data and timing: WITHIN requires repetition within each resampling training partition, and totals or silence about splitting cannot establish OTHER.

round2.revised_rule: Feature selection means a reported data-driven choice of which inputs enter a model fitted in the study, including embedded subset selection or selection for a later fitted model. Ordinary tree-node splitting, literature or theory-based predictor choice, entering all listed predictors, and importance reporting alone do not establish such a step or its absence. Code NA (status not_applicable) only when cited statements establish that no qualifying selection occurred; otherwise code ORDER_NR (status reported) when its occurrence or timing cannot be established. Code WITHIN only when selection is repeated within each resampling training partition; TRAIN when selection uses training data only; BEFORE when selection precedes the split; OTHER for another established arrangement. These assignments require cited statements linking the selection step to the relevant data and timing. Sample totals alone do not establish selection scope, and silence about splitting does not establish that no split occurred. All non-NA response codes have status reported.

From cited statements linking selection to its data and timing, code WITHIN when repeated within each resampling training partition, TRAIN when using training data only, BEFORE when preceding the split, or OTHER for another established arrangement; otherwise code ORDER_NR, including when input choice is unmentioned (all non-NA codes have status reported).

- Code NA (status not_applicable) only when cited statements establish no qualifying selection, such as inputs fixed in advance or all listed inputs entered.
- Code OTHER when cited statements establish selection on the whole analysed sample and no split or resampling is described; record “no split described” without inferring that none occurred. Sample totals alone do not establish selection scope.

round1.proposed_rule: Evaluation data are the data on which the reported performance is computed: a test split, cross-validation or bootstrap evaluation folds, or the development data themselves when only apparent performance is reported. Cross-validation used only for tuning within a training set is not evaluation data. NOT_USED when cited statements or a flow figure establish that at least one data-driven step (e.g. imputation, scaling, outlier removal or capping, count-based category merging, resampling, supervised selection, factor analysis or clustering) used data that include the evaluation data: e.g. done on the whole sample before the split, selection from test-set results, or performance reported only on the same data the step used. USED only when every described data-driven step is stated as fitted on training data only (within each fold for cross-validated estimates). UNC when no step is established as using evaluation data but the data scope of at least one described step is unstated; NR when no data-driven preprocessing step is described; NA only when no performance on any data is reported. Absence of a stated separation is never NOT_USED.

For this item, evaluation data include observations scored for apparent performance, validation, testing or tuning, including held-out tuning folds; this does not classify tuning scores as reported validation performance. Data-driven preprocessing includes separately learned transformations, resampling and predictor selection, including evaluation-informed final predictor retention, but excludes the learner's own fitting operations. Code NOT_USED when cited text or supplementary code establishes that any such step used evaluation observations, and USED only when separation is established for every reported such step, within each relevant resampling partition. Otherwise code UNC when preprocessing or its separation is described but separation cannot be determined, and NR when neither is described; use NA only when statements establish that no performance evaluation exists by design. Record inconsistency only when supplied statements contradict each other about the same step, data and condition.

round1.proposed_rule: An active intervention is a step that changes the training data or the fitting to counter class imbalance: over-, under- or synthetic sampling (e.g. SMOTE), class or sample weights, cost-sensitive loss, or an imbalance-specific ensemble. Stratified splitting or folds, choosing metrics (e.g. PR-AUC), choosing models, or only mentioning that classes are imbalanced are not interventions. If the report and supplement describe no active intervention, code NA (status not_applicable, rationale: 'no active class-imbalance intervention described'). Use ORDER_NR only when an active intervention is described but its timing relative to the split or resampling is not stated. Use WITHIN, TRAIN or BEFORE only when cited text states that timing.

When class-imbalance handling and its timing are unreported, code ORDER_NR with status reported and kind judged under the legacy rules; this does not assert that an intervention occurred. Use NA with status not_applicable and value NA only when the report states or logically establishes that no active intervention exists, never merely because none is described. Class proportions, model or metric choices, other preprocessing, and stratified validation do not by themselves establish an active intervention or its timing.

round1.proposed_rule: Code each component from printed text only, from anywhere in the report (abstract, introduction, methods or discussion). Objective is reported when the report states an aim to develop, evaluate or apply a prediction model, or to identify predictors of the outcome. Target population is reported when the report names the population the model or study is for. The stated eligibility of the analysed sample counts (e.g. 'Korean adults aged 19 years or older'). Intended use is reported only when the report states both of the following about the model or its predictions: (a) a specific purpose, such as screening, triage, diagnosis, risk stratification or a named clinical or public-health decision, and (b) at least one intended user or use setting, such as clinicians, primary care, EHR decision support or health check-ups. The following are not an intended use: saying that the model predicts the outcome, general hopes such as 'prevention', 'early management', 'tailored strategies', 'complement risk assessment', 'inform guidelines' or 'contribute to prediction', and uses proposed for risk factors or findings rather than for the model. Code R only when all three components are reported, P when one or two are, and NR when none is. Name the reported and missing components in the rationale.

Assess all three components at study level using explicit statements anywhere in the report: objective is what the study seeks to investigate, develop or evaluate; intended use is an application expressly attributed to the study or its outputs. Broad, conditional or future applications—including risk assessment, screening, prevention, management or guidance—count without a specified user, setting or decision point; merely restating the prediction task or giving general background benefits does not. An explicitly described study population, including eligibility criteria, or intended beneficiary group counts as target population; no separate deployment population is required, and none may be inferred from the survey name. Enter R when all three components are reported, P when some are reported and NR when none are reported, listing the reported components and their printed basis in the rationale.

round1.proposed_rule: Judge PD_A5 only on the overfitting-prevention methods the report states for that model's development: penalisation or regularisation, dropout, early stopping, pruning or stated complexity limits (depth, leaves, minimum node size, number of rounds), and hyperparameter tuning or early stopping using resampling or a validation split within the development data. None of the following is a prevention method; record each in its own item, and it does not set this code except as stated below for PN: internal validation used only to estimate performance; evaluation on training data; the data scope or leakage of preprocessing, imputation, feature selection or resampling; stepwise or significance-based selection; collinearity screening; sample size; choosing the best model on evaluation results; general descriptions of an algorithm's properties. Codes: NI = no such method is stated for the model. Y = a method is stated, and for every tuned or early-stopped quantity the report states which data were used and that these were kept apart from the evaluation data. PY = a method is stated, but which data it used, or whether it was nested in resampling, is not stated. PN = a method is stated, but a stated step contaminates the data it used (e.g. oversampling or scaling fitted before the tuning folds were formed). N = the report itself states that the model overfitted, or the only stated method used the evaluation data. Give one entry per final or compared model and development dataset as the report names them; use 'all models' only when every model gets the same code.

Proposed clarification; the official instrument and Explanation and Elaboration could not be retrieved for verification. Judge each stated model–development-dataset unit separately, grouping only when the same code applies, and attribute safeguards or defects only to units shown to use them. Explicitly applied, plausibly suitable complexity controls or resampling-based tuning support PY despite missing implementation details; Y requires sufficient evidence of adequacy relative to sample size and model complexity. Use N for established material inadequacy, PN for evidence supporting probable inadequacy, and NI when neither adequacy nor inadequacy can be supported: silence about safeguards or fitting scope does not establish their absence or leakage. A split, performance-only cross-validation, an algorithm name, significance-based selection, an unqualified large sample or favourable observed performance alone does not establish appropriate prevention; established contamination of fitting, selection or tuning counts against adequacy for affected units and is not automatically overcome by a penalty or favourable performance. Code data scope only from statements linking the operation to its data, and record inconsistency only when available statements contradict the same fact, object and condition; fitting a transformation and applying it are different operations.

round1.proposed_rule: Code Y only when the report itself states that the predictors were defined and measured the same way for all participants (and across cycles, sites or examiners where the data have several). Code PY when the report only names a common source, instrument or definition (e.g. the survey questionnaire, the 24-hour recall, raw-data categories) and nothing in it points to differences. Do not infer uniformity from the survey being standardised, because that is general knowledge. Code PN or N only when the report states a difference between participants, cycles or sites, and NI when it says nothing about how the predictors were defined or measured. For this item, record an inconsistency only when two places in the report contradict each other about the definition, coding or measurement of the same predictor. Use present when the report shows they describe the same variable, and uncertain when it does not. Contradictions about participant counts or the number of predictors belong to other items. Units follow the existing PROBAST+AI unit rule.

Use Y when report-specific methods establish common predictor definitions and measurement across the relevant participants; use PY when they support similarity but leave its coverage uncertain, and NI when there is insufficient report-specific information to judge; apply the corresponding distinction to N and PN. A methods description applying to the study participants can establish Y without the literal words 'same for all'; shared survey membership alone cannot, and multiple survey years alone do not establish differences. Conflicting labels, counts or descriptions do not themselves establish different measurement across participants: assess inconsistency separately using the existing same-fact, same-object and same-condition rule. Apply the existing unit rules: include the final/best model and each equally evaluated model on each stated evaluation dataset, use 'all models' when the answer is shared, and do not invent evaluations or subgroup entries.

round1.proposed_rule: Judge the interval against the intended use that the report states for the evaluated model. Treat the use as prediction of a future condition only if the report says so explicitly: incident, future, developing, occurrence (or the Korean term for it), onset, or a time horizon. The words 'predict' or 'risk' alone do not count, and if the report itself says the model identifies prevalent or current status, that statement decides. For a current or detection use, code Y if the report states that predictors and outcome were measured at the same visit or day. Code PY if it states only that both come from the same survey cycle or cross-sectional survey, including a stated short gap within that survey. Code NI only if the report does not state when, or in which survey, predictors and outcome were assessed. For a stated future use, code N if the report states that predictors and outcome come from the same cross-sectional survey or that the outcome was already present at measurement (e.g. a lifetime or past-year history). An exact interval that is not printed is never, by itself, a reason for NI. Give the stated intended use and the timing facts, with their IDs, in the rationale.

Judge the interval for the outcome actually evaluated: detection or estimation of current or recalled status does not require prospective follow-up merely because the report uses prediction, risk or early-detection language; an explicitly future-event target does require a suitable forward interval. Use Y when the stated assessment timing clearly establishes appropriateness, and PY when an explicitly described cross-sectional assessment of the relevant predictors and outcome supports probable appropriateness without establishing the exact interval; do not record simultaneity unless stated. Use NI when only common survey membership, years or components are given, or temporal suitability otherwise cannot be judged; use PN/N only when stated facts support probable/definite inappropriateness, not merely missing timing or a historical outcome label. All response codes retain status reported, and existing evaluation-unit naming rules apply. This operational clarification has not been verified against the official instrument and Explanation and Elaboration, which were inaccessible in this session.

round2.revised_rule: Judge the interval against the intended use that the report states for its own evaluated model. Treat the use as prediction of a future condition only if the report says so explicitly for its own model: incident, future, developing, occurrence (or the Korean term for it), onset, or a time horizon. The words 'predict', 'risk', 'screening' or 'early detection' alone do not count, and neither do such words used about other studies. If the report says its model identifies prevalent or current status, that statement decides. For a current or detection use: Y if the report states that predictors and outcome were measured at the same visit or day; PY if it states only that both come from the same survey, survey cycle or cross-sectional study, including a stated short gap within it. For a stated future use: N if the report states that predictors and outcome come from the same survey or survey cycle, or that the outcome was already present when the predictors were measured (e.g. a lifetime or past-year history); Y if it states that the outcome was assessed after predictor measurement over a follow-up matching the stated horizon; PY if it states a later assessment without giving the length. Code NI only if the report does not state when, or in which survey, predictors and outcome were assessed; a missing exact interval is never, by itself, a reason for NI. Give the stated intended use and the timing facts, with their IDs, in the rationale.

Judge interval appropriateness for the outcome actually evaluated and its stated use. Prediction, risk, early-detection or occurrence wording alone does not establish a future-event target. For current or recalled-status assessment, use Y when stated timing clearly establishes appropriateness, and PY when the report links the relevant predictor and outcome assessments to the same survey cycle or cross-sectional assessment without establishing their exact interval; do not infer simultaneity. An explicitly future-event target requires a suitable forward interval. Use PN/N only when stated facts support probable/definite inappropriateness, and NI when suitability cannot be judged; a missing exact interval or historical outcome label alone does not establish inappropriateness. Cite the evaluated target and timing evidence. Apply the existing legacy-status and evaluation-unit rules.

round1.proposed_rule: The candidate set is the set of variables the report names as the pool from which predictors were selected (by any significance, importance, stepwise or algorithmic step). If the report describes no selection step, it is the full set of inputs the report states were entered into the model(s). Status is reported when the number of that set is printed (kind printed), or when the set is listed exhaustively by name in text or in a table the report identifies as the candidate or input variables (kind derived; give the count per group in the rationale). For this item, a count from such a list is the answer, not a supplementary derived number. Count one per named variable, not dummy levels or the components of a composite score. Include every listed variable unless the report states that it was not offered to the models (e.g. used only for matching, stratification or outcome definition). Status is not_reported when, after describing a selection, the report gives only the selected or final inputs; also when it gives only the features shown in an importance figure, or a non-exhaustive list ('such as', 'among others') with no printed number. Put what is given in the rationale. If two places print different counts for the same set, give both printed values separated by '; ' and set inconsistency present.

Extract the candidate pool before any predictor selection from a stated count or a complete list identified as that pool; downstream model inputs and partial importance displays alone do not establish it, and matching alone does not justify excluding variables. Counting an eligible list is permitted with kind derived, but without a printed candidate count status remains not_reported under the general numeric-status rule; related information alone does not answer the core question. round1.proposed_rule: PE_P1 judges only whether the design of the evaluation data fits the type of the model's outcome and the target population as the report states them. Participant selection, exclusions, missing data and harmonisation belong to other items and do not lower this answer. Decide the outcome's timing from how the report defines it, not from words like 'risk' or 'prediction' or from a comparison with a prognostic score. If the outcome is status measured in the same survey as the predictors (prevalent or current), the model is diagnostic, and a cross-sectional survey that the report describes as representative of the target population is coded Y. Code PY only when the report names the source but does not describe its design or representativeness. Code PN only when the report states that the model is meant to predict a future or incident outcome (e.g. 'incident', 'future', 'within N years') but evaluates it on prevalent cross-sectional data. Code N if the report itself says this mismatch exists. Code NI when the evaluation data source is not described. Apply the same reasoning to every evaluation dataset (internal test, cross-validation, external).

Judge source suitability against the explicitly stated prediction task and population: use Y when the reported information clearly establishes suitability, PY when it supports suitability but leaves a relevant uncertainty (identify it), N/PN for clear/probable incompatibility, and NI when suitability cannot be judged; national representativeness alone does not establish task suitability. Cross-sectional data can support concurrent classification, but cannot establish evaluation of an explicitly incident/future outcome without subsequent outcome ascertainment; generic ‘risk’ or ‘prediction’ wording, comparison with a prognostic score, and recommendations for prospective research do not establish prognostic timing. Use the printed outcome definition and timing, retaining explicit incident wording and leaving unresolved information unresolved rather than assuming either a concurrent or future task. Apply the existing coverage rules: ‘code the final or best model of the study and, where the report evaluates several models equally, each of them’; ‘Give one value entry per unit the report distinguishes’, using ‘all models’ when the same value holds for every included model.

round1.proposed_rule: PE_R3: Not stating blinding is not enough for NI. Judge from what the report says about how the predictors and the outcome were obtained. Code PY when the predictors are objective measurements, or factual or self-reported items collected by the survey's standard procedure, and the outcome is a measurement, score or category obtained separately or derived by the analysts from other variables. This applies even when both come from the same survey wave. Code PN when the cited text shows that whoever recorded a predictor already knew the outcome (e.g. the outcome is a previously diagnosed condition self-reported in the same survey), and at least one predictor is a self-reported behaviour, symptom or perception that this knowledge could affect. Code Y or N only when the report says so explicitly. Code NI only when the report does not describe how the predictors or the outcome were obtained well enough to make this judgement. Whether predictors were measured before or after the outcome, or could have been changed by it, belongs to the timing items, not to PE_R3. Give one entry per model and evaluation dataset. Use 'all models' or 'all datasets' when the value is the same, and do not split entries by subgroup or threshold of the same model and dataset.

Never answer PN from silence (e.g. the report does not say whether predictor selection was repeated within the CV folds -> NI). Code HIGH if any answer is N/PN, LOW if all are Y/PY, else UNC. Stated facts that give N/PN: the performance measures the report names include no calibration measure (calibration plot, slope, intercept, O/E, Hosmer-Lemeshow), or, for a risk or classification model, no discrimination measure (AUROC/C-statistic); accuracy, precision, recall, F1, MAE or RMSE alone do not count. Also: exclusion of participants with missing values from the data the model was evaluated on; a data-driven step (predictor selection, imputation, scaling, tuning) stated to have used data that include the evaluation data or to have been done before or outside the split or resampling loop; performance computed on the training data. Name each unit '<model family> | <dataset>', where dataset is exactly development, internal test, cross-validation, bootstrap or external: <name>, taken from the data the report says the performance was computed on (e.g. 'evaluated on the training data' -> development; not stated -> 'evaluation dataset not stated'), with no further design detail.

round1.proposed_rule: The criterion has an object only when a variable ranking (importance, SHAP, tree splits, coefficients) is used in this study to decide which variables enter, or are removed from, a later model, sensitivity model or tool that this study fits or evaluates. If the ranking is only reported, interpreted or partly displayed (e.g. top k shown), or if variables are selected by another method, code not_applicable (N). Proposals of future models or tools are not a carry-forward step. When there is a carry-forward step, code met only if the report states both the rule or reason (e.g. top k, cut-off, or stated reason for excluding a variable) and the data on which that decision was based (the sample, split or groups the deciding values come from); otherwise not_met.

Code met when the report states both the carry-forward rule and the data informing that decision; a qualitative exclusion reason can supply the rule, and linked statements can identify its supporting data without establishing a particular data split. Otherwise code not_met, with status reported for this legacy item. Do not infer that selection was not done from descriptive rankings, displayed subsets, model-output lists, future proposals or silence: not_applicable requires an established absence of the criterion’s object by design. A stated reason for not doing the step can meet the item; merely not doing it does not make it not_applicable.

round1.proposed_rule: Judge the design against what the model is meant to predict, as the report states it. If the predictors and the outcome come from the same survey round, and the outcome is a current status or history (measured value, test result, or doctor-diagnosis or self-report answer), the design is diagnostic-type: answer Y, unless the report states that the model is meant to predict a future occurrence. Words like 'risk' or 'incidence' used only in results or discussion, or prevention and screening named as a purpose, don't change that. Answer N if the report states the aim as future occurrence, onset or incidence (e.g. the Korean term for occurrence) but the outcome is a status at the same survey. Answer N or PN if participants were selected from the source by outcome status (case-control) without accounting for the sampling fractions. Rebalancing within the training set (under- or oversampling, SMOTE, 1:1 sampling) or matching on something other than the outcome is analysis and doesn't affect this item. Answer NI only when the report gives nothing on how or when the outcome and predictors were recorded.

Assess design against the prediction target established jointly by the stated aim, outcome definition and timing: cross-sectional data can support detection of existing status, whereas future-onset prediction requires an established predictor-before-outcome relationship. Generic words such as risk, prediction, incidence or occurrence, an absent prediction horizon, and limitations about causal inference do not alone establish either target or a mismatch. Use Y or N when the stated facts establish design appropriateness or inappropriateness; use PY or PN when they support that direction but leave a specific relevant uncertainty; use NI when neither direction is supportable, explaining what cannot be determined. Distinguish source-study sampling from model resampling and preprocessing when applying the official design criteria; never state that an adjustment was absent merely because it was not described.

If the outcome is recorded after the predictors (follow-up or linkage), the design is a cohort: answer Y. If the study sample itself was drawn from the source population by outcome status (case-control), answer PN unless the report states that the sampling fractions were accounted for (then Y). round1.proposed_rule: Judge PD_O1 only on how the report defines and determines the target variable the models were actually trained on. Y = the report prints an explicit operational definition: a measured value, a lab or anthropometric cut-off, a validated instrument with a cut-off, a named questionnaire item with the response categories used, a named score with a threshold, or diagnosis or treatment criteria; and the report states no limitation of that definition. Do not mark down for missing assay or measurement-protocol details, for a screening instrument rather than a diagnostic interview, for a single item, or for components or populations the coder thinks are missing from general knowledge. PY = an explicit definition with a limitation or deviation that the report itself states. NI = the outcome is only named (condition names, 'history of'/'prevalence of', class labels, undefined thresholds) without the criterion, item, instrument or measurement that determined it, or the report's places give conflicting target variables or class sets so that the target cannot be fixed. PN/N only when the report states that the outcome was determined in a way that misclassifies it. Do not judge under PD_O1: prevalent or cross-sectional status described as 'incidence' or 'risk', a calculated or surrogate outcome, or overlap between the outcome and the predictors. Record these in the rationale only; they are coded in the design and predictor-outcome items. Give one entry 'all models | development: <dataset as named>' when the value is the same, and separate entries only where values differ.

Assess the reported operational outcome and its assessment method against the explicitly stated prediction target: neither generic risk/incidence wording nor a disease-themed aim alone establishes a future-event target, and neither a questionnaire nor a calculated score alone establishes a screening or proxy target. Use Y when the reported definition and assessment support appropriateness for that target; use PY when they support probable appropriateness but leave an identified, limited uncertainty; use PN or N when reported evidence supports a probably or clearly inappropriate definition, assessment or target mismatch; use NI when essential information is insufficient to support either direction. A single-item or self-reported measure, screening instrument, calculated score, omitted alternative diagnostic criterion or missing laboratory-protocol detail does not by itself determine the response: identify its consequence for assessing the stated target, without assuming unreported validity or procedures. Apply the existing rules literally: use only printed report evidence, not assertions in coder rationales or unprinted continuations; record inconsistency only for contradictory statements about the same fact, object and condition, using uncertain when identity cannot be established. Cover each final or compared model developed on each dataset, distinguishing developments for different outcomes; combine entries only where the same response applies, and retain status reported whenever a legacy response code is assigned.

round1.proposed_rule: A report that states predictors and outcome came from the same survey wave or examination gives the timing (concurrent), so NI is used only when the report gives no source or timing for predictors or outcome. Code PN when the outcome definition states a diagnosis made before the survey or a past reference period (ever or doctor-diagnosed, self-reported 'has the disease', a 12-month reference period), because the predictors were then measured after the outcome. Code N when the report states the model predicts disease that develops after the predictors are measured (incident, future onset, follow-up) but all data come from the same survey. Otherwise (outcome measured at the survey or examination, or stated as current status, including short stated gaps within the survey) code PY. 'Predict', 'risk' or 'occurrence' alone does not make a model a future-onset model.

Judge the reported assessment interval against the outcome target actually modelled: current-status classification does not require prospective follow-up, and words such as 'risk' or 'prediction' alone do not establish a future-event target. Survey membership, cross-sectional design, recall periods, diagnosis history and possible treatment effects alone establish neither the assessment interval nor its appropriateness; do not substitute time since diagnosis for time between assessments. Assign Y/PY or N/PN only when reported timing and the target support that judgement; an exact numerical interval is unnecessary, but otherwise assign NI with status reported. This proposed clarification could not be checked against the official PROBAST+AI instrument and Explanation and Elaboration because those sources were unavailable through the supplied tools.

round1.proposed_rule: Answer each outcome signalling question from printed facts only, then rate the domain: HIGH if all are Y/PY, LOW if any is N/PN, otherwise UNC. O3 (outcome determined without knowledge of predictors): Y if blinding is stated. PY if the outcome is stated to be the participant's own answer to a question, or a device or laboratory reading classified by a fixed cut-off. NI if it needed interpretation by an assessor (grading, examination finding, clinical diagnosis) and blinding or independence from the predictors is not stated. O4 (interval): PY if the report states that outcome and predictors come from the same survey, examination or wave and the stated aim is detecting a current condition. N only if the report states the model predicts future occurrence or risk of developing the condition while the outcome is a diagnosis or condition recorded at the same time as or before the predictors. NI if the report does not state where or when the outcome was recorded. Answer O1/O2 PN/N only for an outcome definition or procedure the report states. If a printed formula or definition conflicts with the standard the report says it followed, answer NI and describe the conflict in the rationale; it is not a critical failure.

Specify the outcome signalling questions, their response criteria and which failures are critical; do not reconstruct these from coder rationales. Assign HIGH when all applicable signals are supported Y/PY, LOW when cited evidence establishes a specified critical failure, and otherwise UNC. Do not infer assessor independence or assessment timing from standardisation or survey membership, or treat missing information, self-report, composite outcomes or concurrent/historical ascertainment as failures by themselves; assess suitability against the stated target. Assess an explicitly applied outcome calculation as printed, without assuming either a correction or a different implementation. Preserve each required model–development-dataset unit, grouping only identical judgements with complete coverage.

final_rule:
For every model | development dataset unit, answer the outcome signalling questions from cited printed facts and record HIGH if all are Y/PY, LOW if any is N/PN (the critical-failure rule), otherwise UNC; missing information is not evidence of failure, every required unit must be covered, and NA applies only when no development object exists by design. - For O4, replace the same-survey/examination/wave PY with N if the report states that the model predicts future occurrence of the condition or the risk of developing it.

round1.proposed_rule: Judge the design against the outcome as the report defines it (what was measured and when), not against wording such as 'predict', 'risk', 'occurrence', 'in advance', or limitation statements about causality or the lack of follow-up; outcome-timing problems belong to the outcome items. Y: the outcome is defined as status present when the predictors were measured (current, prevalent or ever-diagnosed) and the report names the evaluation data as cross-sectional or a population survey. PY: the outcome is defined that way but the report does not name the design of the evaluation data. PN/N: only when the report defines the outcome as an event occurring after predictor measurement and the evaluation data cannot observe it. NI: only when the report states neither the outcome timing nor the evaluation data's design. Give the same value to internal and external evaluations of the same design. When the report does not say which data produced the estimates, or the only CV is part of model fitting, name the unit 'model | evaluation data not specified' and still judge the design of the data source.

Proposed operational wording; the official instrument and Explanation and Elaboration were unavailable for verification: Judge the reported evaluation study design against the explicitly defined prediction target and horizon: cross-sectional observation can establish an appropriate design for classifying contemporaneous status or recorded diagnostic history, whereas future incident-event prediction requires an appropriate temporal design. Generic prediction, risk or prevention language, and limitations concerning causality, do not establish a future-event target; respect any explicitly stated future target rather than silently replacing it with current-status classification. Use Y or N when reported facts establish suitability or unsuitability, PY or PN when they support that conclusion with a specified material uncertainty, and NI when the information needed for the design judgement is insufficient. Never enter a procedure or dataset assignment that the report does not state: fitting/calibration cross-validation alone establishes neither cross-validated performance nor development-set performance. Name units '<family of the model> | <evaluation dataset>'; code the final or best model and, where several models are evaluated equally, each of them, using 'all models' when the same value holds for every eligible model.

An explicitly stated future-event target requires a design capable of observing that event after predictor measurement. Use Y/N when cited facts establish suitability/unsuitability, PY/PN when they support that conclusion with a specified material uncertainty, and NI when necessary information is insufficient. A design label alone does not determine the response. Apply the existing extraction rules: fitting or calibration cross-validation alone establishes neither cross-validated nor development-set performance; use '<model family> | evaluation data not specified' when the evaluation dataset is unidentified. Judge the source design only where the report links that source to the evaluation. Code the final or best model and models evaluated equally, using 'all models' when the same value holds for every eligible model. Give evidence and rationale.

Timing = a stated time point or window of the outcome assessment: either relative to predictor measurement (same visit, follow-up interval) or as a time reference in the outcome's defining phrase (e.g. 'past year', 'current'); survey years, a 'cross-sectional' design, the survey's examination setting or the number of repeated measurements do not count as timing. round1.proposed_rule: A component counts as reported when the report states at least one concrete operation of it for the prediction model's data or predictors. Preprocessing means operations such as recoding/categorisation, derived variables, normalisation/scaling, imputation, outlier or missing-value handling, or balancing. Variable selection means a stated method or basis for choosing the predictors: a test or threshold, a penalised or importance-based selection, exclusion of variables by a criterion, or a statement that predictors were prespecified, taken from literature, or that all available variables were used. Model development means the algorithm(s) with training or tuning procedure. These do not count: a generic label alone ('data cleaning', 'preprocessing'); participant eligibility or exclusion; a list of the predictors used with no basis for choosing them; algorithm-internal feature subsampling (e.g. square-root features per split); statements about other analyses. Code only whether each component is present, not whether it is complete or adequate. Inconsistency for this item covers only contradictions about whether a component was reported. Contradictions in the details of a component (thresholds, counts, model or feature lists) belong to the items that code those details: record none here.

Count each component when at least one specific procedure or explicit decision used in the prediction analysis is stated, including explicit non-use; unexplained additional details do not cancel that evidence. Preprocessing requires a stated operation on the modelling data, such as missing-data handling, recoding, scaling or resampling; population eligibility, outcome definitions and a generic 'data cleaning' label alone do not suffice. Variable selection requires an explicit choice, retention or exclusion of model inputs, whether substantive or data-driven; a bare input list, descriptive tests without a stated selection role, choices for another analysis and random predictor sampling at individual tree nodes do not suffice. Model development requires a statement that an identified prediction model was fitted or trained, rather than generic algorithm exposition alone. Code R when all three components qualify, P when one or two qualify, and NR when none qualifies; put the component list and evidence in the rationale, retain status reported for each response code, and assess inconsistency separately under the existing rules.

round1.proposed_rule: Judge only against an intended moment or setting of use that the report itself states (e.g. lay self-assessment, screening, primary care, clinical decision support, prevention before the event). A description of the modelling task, or the fact that predictors and outcome were measured at the same visit, is not a stated intended use. If no use is stated, the answer is NI. Judge the predictors of the final model as listed; if the final set is not listed, judge the inputs the report says the model was trained with. Y = the report states that these predictors are obtainable in that setting. PY = the setting is stated and nothing in the report says any predictor is unavailable there. PN = the report says obtaining the predictors in that setting is difficult or not routine; or the model uses inputs outside what the report says the intended use relies on (e.g. lab or dietary-recall values in a model stated to use routine body-composition measures or no medical testing); or a model stated for use before the outcome uses a predictor the report describes as a sign, symptom or consequence of the outcome. N = the report states that a predictor is recorded only after the moment of use. Never use general knowledge about what a setting usually collects. Cite the statement of use and the predictor basis in the rationale.

For each model-development dataset, assess its required predictors at the report’s stated intended use: 'never fill from general knowledge or from what is usual for KNHANES' and 'never enter a number, procedure, split or timing that the report does not state.' Use Y when cited statements clearly establish availability of all required inputs, N when they clearly establish nonavailability of at least one, PY/PN when they support the corresponding direction with relevant uncertainty, and NI when neither direction is supported. An explicit statement that the complete inputs are usable in the intended self-assessment supports Y without requiring every predictor’s measurement definition; a screening goal, predictor list or input interface alone does not establish availability. Predictor complexity, contemporaneous survey measurement and possible post-outcome changes alone establish neither availability nor nonavailability; reported collection difficulties bear only on the affected inputs, models and setting, and predictor–outcome overlap remains a separate judgement.
