Judge the predictors of the final model as listed; if the final set is not listed, judge the inputs the report says the model was trained with. Y = the report states that these predictors are obtainable in that setting. PY = the setting is stated and nothing in the report says any predictor is unavailable there. PN = the report says obtaining the predictors in that setting is difficult or not routine; or the model uses inputs outside what the report says the intended use relies on (e.g. lab or dietary-recall values in a model stated to use routine body-composition measures or no medical testing); or a model stated for use before the outcome uses a predictor the report describes as a sign, symptom or consequence of the outcome. N = the report states that a predictor is recorded only after the moment of use. Never use general knowledge about what a setting usually collects. Cite the statement of use and the predictor basis in the rationale.

rule_source: agreed by both systems in round 3
final_rule: For each model-development dataset, assess its required predictors at the report’s stated intended use: 'never fill from general knowledge or from what is usual for KNHANES' and 'never enter a number, procedure, split or timing that the report does not state.' Use Y when cited statements clearly establish availability of all required inputs, N when they clearly establish nonavailability of at least one, PY/PN when they support the corresponding direction with relevant uncertainty, and NI when neither direction is supported. An explicit statement that the complete inputs are usable in the intended self-assessment supports Y without requiring every predictor’s measurement definition; a screening goal, predictor list or input interface alone does not establish availability. Predictor complexity, contemporaneous survey measurement and possible post-outcome changes alone establish neither availability nor nonavailability; reported collection difficulties bear only on the affected inputs, models and setting, and predictor–outcome overlap remains a separate judgement.

round1.proposed_rule: Judge each model only on whether the report states that its printed performance was obtained on data not used to fit it. Y: the text, a table or figure title or label, or the abstract attributes the printed estimates of that model to held-out test, cross-validation, bootstrap or external data (e.g. a heading naming test results, 'test dataset', 'cross-validated risk estimate'). PY: the report states that such an evaluation was done for that model (or evaluation on artificially masked values), but the printed estimates are not explicitly attributed to it. A comparator stated to be run 'the same way' as a model with a described evaluation gets that model's answer. Unstated split sizes, reuse of test data for selection or tuning, and incompletely described repeated runs do not lower Y or PY here, because other items cover them. N: the report states that the estimates come from the fitting data, or the only statistic is the fit statistic of that fitted model (e.g. R² in its own coefficient table) and no validation is described for it. PN: performance is printed and no split, cross-validation, bootstrap or external evaluation is mentioned anywhere for that model. NI: a validation procedure is mentioned, but the report does not let you tell whether that model was evaluated with it.

For each model-development dataset, code Y when cited report statements explicitly establish performance evaluation beyond apparent performance; the evaluation statement need not be repeated beside every estimate, and methodological limitations alone do not change this answer unless they undermine that conclusion. Code PY when positive, applicable evidence supports such evaluation but leaves its use uncertain; tuning-only resampling or repeated runs alone do not establish it. Code N when apparent-only evaluation is established, PN when positive evidence supports probable apparent-only evaluation, and NI when its evaluation basis is unstated: silence about validation is not evidence for N or PN. Apply descriptions and cross-references only to the models and procedures the printed text connects; coder rationales cannot supply missing report statements. Record response codes with status reported, allow grouping only where responses are identical while preserving dataset distinctions, and flag inconsistency only for evidenced contradictions about the same fact, object and condition.

round1.proposed_rule: Judge each model | evaluation dataset only on the preprocessing steps the report states (recoding, categorisation, derivation of variables, deletion, imputation, scaling, encoding). Do not lower the grade because steps the report never mentions might have been done. Code Y when the cited statements show that the stated steps covered the evaluated participants in the same way as the development participants: applied to the whole dataset before the split, or fitted on training data and applied to the evaluation data in the same pipeline. Code PY when the steps are stated and nothing indicates a difference, but the cited statements do not show that the steps reached the evaluated participants. Code N when the report states that a predictor was derived or processed differently for the evaluated participants than for the development participants (e.g. a score calculated from substitute variables in the external data). Code NI when no preprocessing step is stated for that evaluation dataset. A development pipeline does not extend to an external dataset unless the report says so, and a statement of which form the inputs took (categorised or not) is not a description of preprocessing.

Proposed clarification, not independently verified against the official Explanation and Elaboration: Code Y when the cited text establishes common predictor-preprocessing rules for the relevant participants, through an explicit statement or an unambiguously shared procedure; PY when actual preprocessing is described collectively for the relevant data but its common application is supported only indirectly; NI when neither basis exists. A common rule may condition on predictor type or participant characteristics; missing details about additional steps or fitting timing alone do not negate established similarity. Input descriptions, raw or noncategorised values, feature removal alone, and random splitting do not establish similar preprocessing, and procedures stated for one cohort must not be extended to another without supporting text. Apply the existing extraction rules: give an entry for each eligible model evaluation established by the report, do not invent subgroup evaluations or dataset assignments, and do not treat cross-validation used only for tuning as evaluation of reported performance.

round2.revised_rule: Judge each model | evaluation dataset only on the preprocessing steps the report states for participants' predictor values: recoding, categorisation, derivation of variables, exclusion of participants with missing values, imputation, scaling, encoding. Do not lower the grade because steps the report never mentions might have been done. Two kinds of statement are not such steps: removing whole variables (irrelevant, duplicated, mostly missing or constant), and saying which form the inputs took (raw, categorised or not). Code Y when the cited statements show that the stated steps covered the evaluated participants in the same way as the development participants. This holds when the steps are stated for the whole dataset that was later split, folded or resampled into the evaluation data, or when they were fitted on training data and applied to the evaluation data in the same pipeline. Code PY when the steps are stated and nothing indicates a difference, but the cited statements do not show that the steps reached the evaluated participants. Code N when the report states that a predictor was derived or processed differently for the evaluated participants than for the development participants (e.g. a score calculated from substitute variables in the external data). Code NI when no such step is stated for that evaluation dataset. Steps stated for the development data do not extend to an external dataset unless the report says so.

Judge similarity of the stated predictor preprocessing across development and evaluated participants. Code Y when explicit statements or an unambiguously shared procedure establish common rules; PY when actual preprocessing is described for the relevant data and cited text supports, but does not establish, common application; N or PN when cited text establishes or supports probable differences, respectively; otherwise NI. Common rules may condition on predictor type or participant characteristics. Unmentioned steps and unspecified fitting timing alone do not lower the response. Input-format descriptions, feature removal alone and random splitting do not establish similar preprocessing. Do not extend procedures beyond their stated data scope or infer different processing merely because one cohort’s procedure is undescribed. Apply the existing unit, validation, evidence and legacy-status rules without adding evaluation assignments.

round1.proposed_rule: Judge availability only against the intended use printed in the report: any stated aim or proposed use (e.g. screening, early warning, detection, prevention, choosing priority groups, a stated setting) counts as the intended use; no exact time point is needed. Code NI only if no intended use is stated or the evaluated model's predictors are not named or defined. Code PN if (a) the report states that some of the model's predictors are hard or impossible to obtain at the intended use (only for the models whose predictors the statement covers); (b) a predictor is a survey-design or administrative variable (survey weights, survey year, IDs); or (c) the intended use comes before the outcome (prevention, early or pre-diagnosis prediction) and the report names a predictor as a diagnosis, treatment, sign or consequence of the outcome. Otherwise, code PY when the predictors are named and nothing printed says they are unavailable; code Y only when the report itself states that all predictors are available at the intended use. Do not use your own view of what is routinely collected, or how KNHANES measured a variable, as a reason for PN. When a detection model's predictors overlap the outcome definition, code that under the overlap item, not here.

For each eligible final/best model–evaluation unit, judge availability from cited report statements about its required predictors and stated intended use: Y/PY require support for availability of all required predictors, N/PN require support for unavailability of at least one, and otherwise use NI (status reported); definite versus probable responses must reflect the evidence. Do not invent a prediction time or infer availability or unavailability from survey collection, possible collectability, collection burden, variable names, or predictor–outcome overlap alone. Apply the existing final/best/equally evaluated model rules, include only established evaluations, exclude tuning-only resampling, and assess predictor-list contradictions separately under the existing same-object inconsistency criteria.

round1.proposed_rule: Code a method only when the report prints its output for a prediction model of the study: a ranking, importance scores, an importance or explanation plot, or a statement naming the most important or influential predictors or their contributions. An interpretable model's own structure counts when the report uses it in this way. Code COEFFICIENT_STATISTIC for coefficients, odds ratios, log OR/LR or nomogram points derived from them; code TREE_RULE for tree splits or rules, e.g. 'the first split is the most important factor'. A model that is only shown (a tree diagram, a list of rules, a nomogram) with no statement about importance gives NA. Importance used only inside predictor selection (LASSO, RFE, Boruta, gain-based elimination) counts only if its ranking or scores are printed; selected or rejected lists alone do not count. Code MODEL_NATIVE only when the report names a built-in measure (Gini, gain, F-score). Code a printed ranking whose measure is not named as OTHER and describe it in the rationale. A score that rescales or combines one method's output keeps that method's code. Analyses that do not explain a prediction model (correlation or network centrality) are not coded. NETWORK_SPECIFIC means methods for neural networks only. Status is not_applicable (NA) when no method qualifies.

Count methods stated to have been used to assess predictor contributions or explain fitted prediction-model outputs, including intrinsic interpretations: coefficient/statistic-based contributions or nomogram points are COEFFICIENT_STATISTIC, and explicitly interpreted fitted trees or rules are TREE_RULE; model construction or a rule listing alone does not qualify. Feature-selection procedures and their internal calculations qualify only when importance or explanation results are also presented; an importance ranking qualifies, whereas selected/rejected decisions alone do not, and a separate association network does not qualify without a stated link to explaining the prediction model. Classify only the procedure stated, without inferring its calculation from model or software names; a reported ranking from a described procedure whose importance calculation is unspecified is OTHER, with the printed basis and limitation described in the rationale. Rescaling or aggregating an importance measure, including combining it with its own rank, retains the underlying method code without adding OTHER. Record each qualifying code once at study level, and apply the existing status rules: excluded material or another item's code does not establish that explanation was not done.

round1.proposed_rule: Give one list for the study. Use the final or best model the authors interpret, from the main analysis. If the report evaluates several models equally and names no final model, use the authors' own summary statement across the models. Never build a union, chain or merge of several models' or sub-populations' rankings. Source and length: take the variables the authors' text explicitly names as most important for that model, in the text's order and only as many as the text names. Prefer the results text; otherwise use the first explicit statement. If the text names none, take the table or figure that the authors title as that model's top-N or ranked importance, in its printed order. If a table with printed importance values and a figure differ, use the table. Do not append rankings within a subset of variables (e.g. 'among X-related features') or loose later mentions (a variable described as one of the most important). Copy names as printed in the source used. If another source gives a different order for the same model and statistic, record inconsistency present. If the only importance information is a decision tree's split variables or its 'best predictor', or regression coefficients, there is no ranking: status not_reported, values empty, and the named variables go in the rationale. This is never not_applicable.

An explicit model-based statement identifying a variable as best or next in importance is a qualifying relative ranking, including prose explaining a decision tree; the exclusion concerns diagrams and split variables alone. Include every explicitly identified most-important, key, major or top-k set across reported models and samples, including sets identified in tables or figures; do not select only the best model or treat every variable in a generic importance display as explicitly selected. Combine qualifying sets into one study-level list, retaining each variable once in first-appearance order through the main report and then supplements, using printed order within each source; this is presentation order, not an inferred pooled importance ranking. Copy printed names and merge differently named variables only when the report establishes their identity; include nothing supported only by a coder's description. Preserve alternative source-specific orders in the rationale when they differ. Apply the existing inconsistency rule: different subset sizes or model/sample rankings are not contradictions; mark present only for incompatible rankings of the same object under the same conditions, and uncertain when their identity cannot be established.

final_rule:
List all variables explicitly identified as most important, key, major, best/next in importance or a top-k set through a model-based ordering or relative-importance comparison, across all reported models and samples, including text, tables and figures. round1.proposed_rule: Eligible importance output is any printed importance value or ranking, any statement naming the most important or leading predictors, or the variables a fitted model keeps together with its structure (a decision tree's splits, a network's arcs). Code NA only when none of these exists. USED requires that the report compares this output for the same model type across resamples (including bootstrap or fold retention frequencies of variables or arcs), survey cycles, participant subgroups, or sensitivity analyses (e.g. alternative inclusion thresholds). These are not comparisons of importance: stability checks of risk estimates or performance, comparisons across algorithms or between odds ratios and importance, importance displayed per outcome class, and separate models for different outcomes. When importance output exists and no such comparison is printed, code NOT_USED, not NR.

Eligible importance output is a printed predictor-contribution score, importance ordering, or explicit qualitative identification of leading or prioritized predictors; a tree caption, selected-variable list or network structure alone is insufficient. USED requires an explicit comparison of eligible importance across resamples, cycles, subgroups or sensitivity analyses, including a clearly labelled comparative figure; performance comparisons, ranking computation, and changes in variable or arc inclusion alone do not qualify. NOT_USED requires explicit nonassessment or a single documented eligible ranking per model/outcome: a lone displayed ranking meets this condition only if the text does not also document additional rankings, including fold-specific rankings; otherwise, unreported stability assessment is NR. Use UNC for an ambiguously described importance comparison and NA when no eligible importance output exists; give one study-level response code, with status reported except for NA, which is not_applicable. Apply the existing evidence and inconsistency rules exactly: include eligible supplementary evidence, and do not infer an importance ranking or contradiction from figure order that the report does not identify as a ranking.

final_rule: Eligible importance output is a printed predictor-contribution score, importance ordering, or explicit qualitative identification of leading or prioritized predictors; a tree caption, selected-variable list or network structure alone is insufficient. USED requires an explicit comparison of eligible importance across resamples, cycles, subgroups or sensitivity analyses, including a clearly labelled comparative figure; performance comparisons, ranking computation, and changes in variable or arc inclusion alone do not qualify. NOT_USED requires explicit nonassessment or a single documented eligible ranking per model/outcome: a lone displayed ranking meets this condition only if the text does not also document additional rankings, including fold-specific rankings; otherwise, unreported stability assessment is NR. Use UNC for an ambiguously described importance comparison and NA when no eligible importance output exists; give one study-level response code, with status reported except for NA, which is not_applicable. Apply the existing evidence and inconsistency rules exactly: include eligible supplementary evidence, and do not infer an importance ranking or contradiction from figure order that the report does not identify as a ranking.

round1.proposed_rule: A compared ranking exists only where the report states that predictor importance, ranking or order (e.g. SHAP, importance scores, first splits, nomogram points, priority order) from two or more analyses was compared, and says what differed or stayed the same. Importance values printed side by side, e.g. per outcome class in one figure, without a stated comparison do not count. Neither do comparisons of something other than predictor importance, such as network arcs, structure-inclusion thresholds or risks of outcome combinations. Status follows the same report's VI16 code: USED -> reported; UNC -> unclear, with the comparison cited; NOT_USED or NA -> not_applicable. The value lists every factor across which the report states such a comparison, separated by '; '. Each factor is named as a category (resamples, survey cycles or datasets, subgroups, outcomes, models or model specifications, sensitivity analyses) followed by the printed levels (kind judged).

An eligible comparison explicitly contrasts predictor-importance values or rankings, including stated top predictors, in text or a comparative display; no formal stability statistic is required. Group labels, selected-variable lists, tree split positions, prediction points, diagnostic-combination risks, or network structure alone do not establish such a comparison. When VI16 is USED, record every stated dimension varied, including outcomes, treatment contrasts, or interpretation methods: the parenthetical examples are not exhaustive. Apply the existing study-level scope across eligible comparisons in the report, and do not infer comparisons or their absence from incomplete evidence.

round2.revised_rule: A compared ranking exists only where the report states in text that predictor importance values, rankings, priority order or top predictors from two or more analyses were compared, or states what differed or stayed the same between them. These do not count: values printed side by side (e.g. per outcome class in one figure) without such a statement; anything the report does not present as predictor importance or ranking (tree split positions, nomogram or prediction points, selected-variable lists, risks of factor combinations, network arcs or arc-inclusion thresholds). If at least one such comparison is stated, VI16 is USED and status is reported; otherwise status is not_applicable. The value lists every factor varied across the stated comparisons, separated by '; '. Name each factor as a category (resamples; survey cycles or datasets; subgroups; outcomes; models, model specifications or interpretation methods; treatment contrasts; sensitivity analyses; or another factor as stated) followed by the printed levels (kind judged).

round1.proposed_rule: Judge only whether the source's design fits the outcome's timing. Use Y when the report names the source, states its design (e.g. a nationally sampled or representative cross-sectional survey) and the outcome is a status measured in the same survey as the predictors. Use PY when the source is named but its design is stated only by citation or not at all. Use PN or N when the outcome is a future event and the data have no follow-up. Wording about prevention, prediction of 'developing' disease, survey vs cohort, or generalisability does not change the answer; those belong to other items. Use PN when the development data pool sources that were sampled or recruited differently (e.g. a convenience or recruited group combined with survey controls), so the case-mix and outcome prevalence come from how the sources were combined. Use NI when the report does not establish which data the models were developed on (e.g. the data described in the methods are not linked to the named source). Never judge a mismatch from outside knowledge of what the source contains. Inconsistency between the two places is 'uncertain' when they may refer to different data.

Under the official PROBAST+AI guidance, judge the reported source and sampling design against the outcome actually modelled and the explicitly stated prediction task; generic prediction or prevention wording does not establish a future-outcome task. Use Y when the description establishes suitability, PY when suitability is probable but a material source-specific uncertainty remains, PN/N when reported evidence supports probable/definite unsuitability, and NI when the available information does not support a directional judgement. A sufficiently described population survey can warrant Y for current-status classification; secondary use, cross-sectional design, limited causal inference, and missing nonessential details do not themselves warrant downgrading. Incompletely linked acquisition descriptions warrant NI when they prevent judging suitability; pooling sources or defining groups by source does not by itself establish inappropriate sampling or distorted outcome prevalence.

round2.revised_rule: Judge whether the source and its design, as the report describes them, fit the outcome as modelled. Y: the report names the source and, in its own text, states how the source was sampled or that it is representative (e.g. 'nationally representative', stratified or multistage probability sampling; 'nationwide' alone does not state the sampling). The outcome must also be a current status measured in the same survey as the predictors. PY: the same, except the design is given only by citation or not at all. PN or N: the outcome is a future event and the data have no follow-up. Also PN: the development data pool sources that were sampled or recruited differently (e.g. a recruited or convenience group combined with survey controls), so case-mix and outcome prevalence depend on how the sources were combined. NI: the report does not establish which data the models were developed on (e.g. the data described in the methods are not linked to the named source). In that case, set inconsistency to 'uncertain' when the two descriptions may refer to different data. Wording about prevention, 'developing' disease, survey versus cohort, limits on causal inference or generalisability does not change the answer. Never judge a mismatch from outside knowledge of what the source contains. When all models share the same source and answer, give one entry 'all models | <development dataset>'.

final_rule:
Code Y when the report identifies the development source and shows that the modelled outcome is a current status measured with the predictors in the same participants in the same survey, even without sampling or representativeness wording; use PY only when a concrete source-related uncertainty stated in the report remains. - Use PN/N for a modelled future event when reported evidence establishes no follow-up, according to probable/definite unsuitability; also use PN when development pools sources explicitly described as sampled or recruited differently, making case-mix and outcome prevalence depend on their combination.
- Use NI when the report does not establish which data were used for development, including acquisition descriptions insufficiently linked to the named source; mark inconsistency uncertain only when descriptions possibly conflict but may concern different data.

round1.proposed_rule: Answer Y when the report states one outcome definition for all participants: criteria, thresholds, the questions with response coding, or the composite rule or the algorithm that assigns the label. The report must also state nothing indicating that the outcome was determined differently for some participants. Answer PY when such a definition is stated and the report itself says that some participants' outcome was determined from different components, sources, criteria, questionnaire versions or ways of reaching a diagnosis (for example, classified from only some of the components). Answer PN or N when it says the difference is substantial. Do not lower Y because of differences the report does not state, such as possible wording changes across survey cycles. Also do not lower it because of misclassification limits that apply equally to everyone, such as single measurements or self-report. Answer NI when the report names the outcome but prints no defining criteria or ascertainment method, or when the cited text does not say what the models' target is. A single survey, a standardised survey design, or a procedure that the text does not link to the models' target is not enough for Y or PY.

Proposed operational clarification; the official instrument and Explanation and Elaboration could not be independently verified. Apply the existing instruction, 'Code only what the report and its supplementary material state': establish the prediction target and its ascertainment from outcome-specific text; survey membership alone is insufficient, and label generation must be linked to that target. Code Y when the report describes a common operational definition and assessment method for the development participants, such as specified questions and response coding, measured-variable classification criteria, or a linked target-label algorithm; a separate declaration of sameness across participants or years is unnecessary. Code PY when outcome-specific evidence supports comparable definition and assessment but leaves comparability incompletely established, NI when there is insufficient outcome-specific evidence to judge comparability, and PN/N when the text supports probable/clear material differences between participants. Missing details that do not affect comparability, hypothetical survey changes, self-report, general misclassification concerns, or possible missing components alone do not justify downgrading; never reconstruct unprinted thresholds, label mappings, procedures, or differential assessment.

round1.proposed_rule: Judge from how the report says the outcome was obtained. If no assessor had to interpret the outcome, give PY when blinding is not stated, and Y only when the report states that the outcome was determined without predictor information. This covers: a measured value compared with a fixed cut-off; a participant's own questionnaire answer (symptom, behaviour, self-rating, physician-diagnosis or medication history) recoded by a stated fixed rule; and any composite made only of such parts. Give NI only when determining the outcome needed an assessor's interpretation (e.g. clinical adjudication, record review, image reading, coding of free text) and the report does not say whether that assessor knew the predictors. Give PN or N only when the report states or shows that predictor values were known or used by whoever assigned the outcome. A predictor that is part of the outcome definition or sets its cut-off (e.g. a sex-specific threshold, a component of the measured value) belongs to the predictor-in-outcome-definition item and does not on its own make this item PN or N; mention it in the rationale. Give one entry 'all models | <development dataset>' when the value is the same for every model.

final_rule:
Code PY when the report describes outcome determination without assessor interpretation—a measured value compared with a fixed cutoff, a participant’s own questionnaire response recoded by a stated fixed rule, or a composite consisting only of these—and blinding is unstated; code Y only when the report states that outcome determination occurred without predictor information. Code NI when the report does not describe how the outcome was determined, or when determination required assessor interpretation and the assessor’s knowledge of predictors is unstated.

- Use PN or N only when the report states or establishes that whoever assigned the outcome knew or used predictor values.
- A predictor’s inclusion in the outcome definition or use in setting its cutoff does not alone justify PN or N; record that fact in the predictor-in-outcome-definition item and mention it in the rationale.

round1.proposed_rule: Judge whether the outcome was the same for participants within each evaluated dataset. Y: the report states one outcome definition or procedure (criterion, instrument, threshold, derived variable, or one data-driven labelling such as a single clustering run on the whole data) for all participants of that dataset, and nothing in the report shows that the definition, instrument, method or timing differed between them; missing measurement details or an evaluation split that is not described do not lower Y. PY or PN: the report gives only partial or indirect signs that the outcome was or was not the same for everyone. N: the report states different definitions or methods for different participants in the dataset. NI: the report gives no outcome definition or method. Records made by resampling (e.g. SMOTE) are not participants: judge real participants only and mention the synthetic records in the rationale. A difference between the development data and the evaluation dataset goes in the rationale, not in this item.

Proposed clarification, pending verification against the official PROBAST+AI instrument and Explanation and Elaboration: Within each model–evaluation dataset, use Y when the report establishes a common outcome definition and comparable assessment for its participants; use PY when relevant evidence supports similarity but comparable assessment is incompletely established, and NI when the relevant outcome or evidence supporting similarity cannot be identified. A common variable or cut-off alone does not establish identical assessment procedures; use PN or N when the report supports probable or established differences in outcome definition or assessment. Prespecified subgroup-specific thresholds can constitute one common definition, and synthetic sampling alone does not establish different assessment of participants’ outcomes; differences confined to predictor measurement or other evaluation datasets do not establish differences within the evaluation being judged. Require an explicit link before using generated clusters as evidence about a classifier’s outcome. Apply the existing final/best-model selection and evaluation-unit rules, aggregate identical responses using the permitted shared unit labels, and leave unstated model–dataset assignments unstated.

round2.revised_rule: Within each model–evaluation dataset, code Y when the report establishes a common outcome definition and similar assessment for its participants; identical procedures and exhaustive measurement details are not required. Use PY or PN when partial or indirect evidence supports probable similarity or dissimilarity, N when dissimilarity is established, and NI when there is no usable evidence to judge similarity. A shared cut-off or variable name alone supports the definition but does not necessarily establish similar assessment. Subgroup-specific thresholds within one common definition and synthetic sampling alone do not establish dissimilarity. Apply the existing model-selection, unit and no-unsupported-inference rules: do not infer a classifier’s outcome from a separate clustering analysis or assign unstated evaluation datasets. Differences confined to predictor measurement or other evaluation datasets do not establish dissimilarity within the evaluation being judged.

final_rule:
Within each model–evaluation dataset, code Y when the report explicitly gives both a common outcome definition and a common assessment method (measurement procedure, instrument or questions) for all participants; code PY when only a common definition is reported and no dissimilarity is described, or partial or indirect evidence supports probable similarity. Code PN for probable dissimilarity supported by partial or indirect evidence, N for established differences in outcome definition or assessment among participants, NI when no usable outcome definition or assessment information is given, and NA only when the item has no object.
Exceptions:
- Treat a single data-driven labelling procedure as one outcome definition; exclude synthetic records from the participant comparison and mention them in the rationale.
- Missing evaluation-split descriptions alone do not warrant NI; differences between development and evaluation datasets belong in the rationale and do not establish dissimilarity within the evaluation dataset.

round1.proposed_rule: Grade each evaluation on how missing data were handled in that evaluation's own data. Internal test and cross-validation sets inherit the handling applied to the sample before the split; an external set is graded on its own stated handling. Use these grades. N: the report states that any participants were excluded because of missing predictor or outcome data (complete-case), whatever the amount and even if imputation was also used. PN: no such exclusion, but missing values were filled with a simple single value (mean, median, mode or constant). PY: no such exclusion, and model-based single imputation was used (e.g. k-nearest-neighbour, random forest, regression). Y: the report states there were no missing data, or multiple imputation was used with no such exclusion. NI: the report says nothing about how missing data were handled. An unreported missing amount, mechanism or implementation detail never makes the answer NI and never changes the grade. For an outcome that is not time-to-event, censoring is not considered.

For each model evaluation, apply the official PE_A2 guidance to the reported handling of missing predictors and outcomes and, when relevant, censoring; development procedures inform this judgement only where the report connects them to that evaluation. Neither complete-case exclusion nor single imputation automatically warrants PN/N, and neither a small exclusion proportion nor naming an imputation algorithm automatically warrants Y/PY: assess the reported extent, reasons, procedure and relevant justification in the evaluation context. Use Y/N when the evidence establishes appropriate/inappropriate handling, PY/PN when it supports that direction with residual uncertainty, and NI when it supports neither direction; unreported safeguards are not established failures, and missing detail does not automatically invalidate an otherwise supported directional judgement.

round2.revised_rule: Grade each model evaluation by the missing-data handling the report states for the data that formed that evaluation set. This includes exclusions made when the cohort was built, before any split. Internal test and cross-validation sets take the handling applied before the split. An external set is graded on the handling stated for it. N: the report states that any participants were excluded because of missing, unknown or invalid predictor or outcome data, or that the sample was limited to participants with complete, valid or answered data (complete-case). This holds whatever the amount, and even if imputation was also used. PN: there was no such exclusion, and missing values were filled with a simple single value (mean, median, mode or constant). PY: there was no such exclusion, and model-based single imputation was used (e.g. k-nearest-neighbour, random forest, regression). Y: the report states there were no missing data, or multiple imputation was used with no such exclusion. NI: the report says nothing about how missing data were handled. When several handlings apply, give the lowest grade. An unreported missing amount, mechanism or implementation detail never makes the answer NI and never changes the grade. Censoring counts only for time-to-event outcomes. There, if censored participants were excluded or counted as non-events, the grade is N. Otherwise censoring does not change the grade.

final_rule:
For each model evaluation, grade the handling reported for its evaluation data, including cohort-building exclusions and pre-split handling that applied to internal test or cross-validation data; use the handling stated for each external dataset. Assign N for complete-case restriction or exclusions due to missing, unknown or invalid predictor/outcome data; PN for simple single-value imputation; PY for model-based imputation, including mice, unless explicitly described as multiple imputation; Y for explicitly stated multiple imputation or no missing data; and NI when handling is unreported or mentioned without an identifiable method; take the lowest applicable directional grade when several methods apply, do not change an otherwise supported grade for unreported amounts, mechanisms or implementation details, and consider censoring only for time-to-event outcomes, assigning N if censored participants were excluded or treated as non-events.

- Change N for missing-data exclusions to PN only when the report states that excluded and included participants were compared and found similar.
- Record selection of an imputation method using test AUC in the rationale without changing the grade.

round1.proposed_rule: A class-imbalance adjustment is a step the report presents as handling class imbalance or as balancing the classes for a model: over- or undersampling, SMOTE or other synthetic samples, class weights or cost-sensitive learning. Merging outcome categories and eligibility exclusions do not count unless the report says they were done to balance the classes. Judge each unit by the adjustment stated for that model. If none is stated, code NI, and do not infer an unadjusted or adjusted evaluation from class counts or prevalence. Code NA only when the report states, or cited statements establish, that the model was trained without adjustment. If an adjustment was done, code Y or N when the report states which data it was applied to (for example 'applied to the training set only' or 'test data used unaltered' -> Y; 'applied before the split' -> N). The order of the text alone is not timing. Code PY or PN when only printed numbers show the evaluation distribution: evaluation n or class counts that match the original data (PY), or that contain synthetic or removed records, or equal classes (PN). Exact performance arithmetic that implies a 50:50 test set also gives PN (for example accuracy equal to the mean of sensitivity and specificity, with the formula in the rationale). Printed counts outweigh a conflicting general statement and give PN. If none of this is available, code NI. Code only the internal test, cross-validation and external units, not development/apparent performance.

Proposed wording; the official instrument and Explanation and Elaboration were unavailable for independent verification: Apply this item separately to each supported model–evaluation unit under the existing model-selection and unit rules; neither a data split alone nor tuning resampling establishes an eligible performance evaluation. Code NA only when the report states or logically establishes that the model used no class-imbalance adjustment; silence is NI, and category merging or eligibility exclusions alone establish neither adjustment nor its absence. When adjustment is established, code Y or N when linked statements or an explicitly labelled workflow establish evaluation in the unadjusted or adjusted distribution, respectively; adjustment confined to training with a separate unadjusted evaluation pathway establishes Y, while evaluation drawn from an explicitly adjusted pool establishes N. round1.proposed_rule: A derived predictor is a model input that the report states or shows the authors constructed from other data: computed by a formula, cut into categories, regrouped or recoded, or combined from several source items. None of the following is a derived predictor: a survey variable used as the survey supplies it, under its own name or description (including the survey's own computed variables); a survey-item definition; encoding, scaling or normalisation; a predictor that is only named or labelled (e.g. 'diabetes (yes, no)', 'current smoker', 'BMI'), unless the report says the authors derived it. Do not infer a derivation from general knowledge. met = the report gives a rule for every derived predictor: a formula, cut-offs, a stated method such as 'quartiles' or a cited criterion, or the source categories of each new category. not_met = at least one derived predictor has no rule, e.g. it is shown as built from named source items, or 'defined using survey questions', with no formula, cut-off or categories. not_applicable = the report shows no derived predictor.

Count substantive predictor calculations, combinations, conversions, category groupings or operational cutoffs explicitly described in the report, whether survey-provided or investigator-created; do not infer additional derivations from variable names, codes, units or score labels, and exclude routine encoding, scaling and normalization. Code met when at least one such predictor is identified and rules are reported for every identified derivation: a formula, cutoff, stated category or quantile grouping, or operational definition suffices, but an output unit alone does not specify a conversion. Otherwise code reported with value not_met, including when derivation is unaddressed. Use not_applicable only when cited statements establish that no such predictors exist.

round1.proposed_rule: Predictor preprocessing means steps that act on the predictor data after the predictors are defined. These are cleaning or outlier handling, imputation, encoding or categorisation, transformation, scaling and harmonisation. Participant exclusion for missing data, class resampling (undersampling, oversampling, SMOTE) and formulas that define or derive a predictor belong to other items and do not count here. Y = the report states that the same preprocessing was applied to all participants or datasets (e.g. 'recoded identically', 'applied unchanged'). PY = every preprocessing step the report mentions is named with its method or rule, it is applied to the whole development data, and the report does not describe any step that differs between participants. NI = no preprocessing step is described, or a mentioned step has no method stated (e.g. 'data cleaning', 'pre-processed', 'imputation' alone). PN = a step is stated to be computed from, or applied to, only one outcome class or subgroup. N = the report states that groups of participants were preprocessed with different rules.

Proposed clarification, pending verification against the official Explanation and Elaboration, which was unavailable: Assess predictor derivation, recoding, transformation, scaling, imputation and outlier handling within each model–development dataset; stated conditional definitions can constitute common rules, while eligibility exclusions, class balancing and file handling alone do not establish similarity. Use Y when participant-wide similarity is explicitly established, PY when concrete common predictor-processing rules provide positive but incomplete evidence of similarity, and NI when that evidence is absent; use N or PN only when cited text establishes or positively supports differential processing, respectively. Do not infer uniformity from pooled data or silence, or differential application merely from a cutoff’s reference group or changed group counts. Apply the existing inconsistency rule separately: contradictory definitions for the same predictor under the same condition are an inconsistency, without automatically changing the similarity judgement.

round1.proposed_rule: Code each scheme the report describes as producing the reported performance estimates. Resampling used only for tuning, predictor selection or confidence intervals is not validation (e.g. bootstrap replicates giving only a mean and 95% CI on a fixed evaluation set are not BOOT; BOOT means models refitted on bootstrap samples and evaluated). APPARENT only when the report states or the cited statements establish that the estimates were computed on the data used to fit the model (a training/development row, the same sample named for fitting and evaluation, or a fit statistic such as explanatory power/R2 of the fitted model); performance printed without naming the evaluation data is NONE_NR. A split of the same survey by year or cycle is TEMPORAL only (not SPLIT, not EXTERNAL); SPLIT is a single random or unspecified train-test split. A split repeated n times with averaged results is OTHER ('repeated random split xn'), with SPLIT added only when single-split estimates are also reported; any other described evaluation scheme (e.g. simulated users, 'n random repeated experiments') is OTHER, described with the printed wording and without inferring what was randomised. Code the described procedure, not the report's label (a repeated split of the same data called 'external' is OTHER, not EXTERNAL). For this item, inconsistency covers only places that conflict about which validation scheme produced the estimates; differing performance values or counts belong to other items.

Code only evaluation procedures stated or logically established: APPARENT requires evaluation on the fitting observations; performance values alone do not establish it, bootstrap means/CIs alone do not establish BOOT validation, and unspecified random repetitions establish no additional method. Selection- or tuning-only resampling is excluded; an explicitly described evaluation outside the named categories is OTHER, described in the rationale. For each holdout procedure use one code: SPLIT for a single internal holdout, replaced by TEMPORAL when chronological separation is established; EXTERNAL for an established separate external evaluation dataset or cycle; OTHER for explicitly repeated random holdouts. A partition of the same study data is not external, and different cycle names alone establish neither externality nor chronological separation; combine codes only for distinct established evaluation procedures. If none is established, use NONE_NR with status reported, retaining unresolved evaluation status rather than inferring nonuse. round1.proposed_rule: Code means source code written for this study. The following are not study code: pseudocode, algorithm figures, and links to third-party packages or libraries the study used. If they are all the report gives, code NOT_PROVIDED_OR_NOT_REPORTED and mention them in the rationale. If the study's code itself is printed in the input (main text or supplementary material), code PUBLIC_ACCESS_VERIFIED. If the code sits only at a link or repository whose content is not in the input, code PUBLIC_LINK_REPORTED_ACCESS_NOT_REVERIFIED. Code LINK_INACCESSIBLE only when the input records a failed access attempt. Code PARTIAL_CODE_ONLY only when the report itself states that just part of the study code is shared, including when part is public and the rest is on request. Never code it from your own judgment of whether the shared code is complete or runs. Code AVAILABLE_ON_REQUEST only when no study code is public and the report offers it on request.

Code availability concerns the study's analysis source code: pseudocode and links identified only as package or backbone implementations do not qualify; if nothing else supplies or offers study code, use NOT_PROVIDED_OR_NOT_REPORTED. Use AVAILABLE_ON_REQUEST when study analysis code is offered on request, even when such resources are publicly linked; reserve PARTIAL_CODE_ONLY for study code explicitly supplied as only part of the analysis without an availability route for the remainder. Extract the stated scope; do not infer partial availability from omitted workflow stages or apparent execution defects. A reported public link to study code receives PUBLIC_LINK_REPORTED_ACCESS_NOT_REVERIFIED unless the input documents successful or failed public access, supporting PUBLIC_ACCESS_VERIFIED or LINK_INACCESSIBLE respectively; code reproduced in the supplied material alone does not verify public access.

Model(s): at least one model type is named. Principal result(s): at least one result on the prediction model's performance, either a printed performance value or a stated performance finding (e.g. which model performed best). Risk-factor or predictor-selection findings, the construction of a nomogram or model, or a statement that the model was verified or validated without giving the result do not count. R = all four components, P = one to three, NR = none; list the components found in the rationale. round1.proposed_rule: USED requires an importance or explanation output that is separate from the model's own structure and that the report presents as such: a printed score, ranking table or plot of importance values (e.g. permutation, Gini/impurity, %IncMSE, gain, SHAP, LIME, partial dependence). A decision tree's diagram, its splits or rules, and verbal rankings read from its root and split order ('most important', 'next') are the model itself, not an importance method, even when the authors say the tree was used to assess importance. These cases are NOT_USED when the tree is the only such output. Coefficients or odds ratios of a conventional regression do not qualify. If coefficients are called the importance of an ML model but the report does not make clear whether they come from that model or from a conventional regression, code UNC. Code NOT_USED when the report describes its analysis and results and no importance or explanation method or output appears anywhere. Code NR only when the report does not describe the analysis or results that would contain it (e.g. abstract only). NA only when the study has no model with input variables; a continuous, regression or unsupervised task is not NA.

Count a fitted tree as USED when the report explicitly presents it to identify influential predictors or explain predictor–outcome rules and supplies the tree or rules; separate importance scores or post-hoc methods are unnecessary. A tree displayed only for prediction or a generic claim of interpretability is insufficient, and coders must not infer importance rankings from split position. An explicitly model-attributed coefficient-based importance ranking also qualifies: extract the stated procedure without judging its technical validity; conventional association coefficients alone do not qualify. Apply NA with status not_applicable outside classification; otherwise reserve NOT_USED for explicit nonuse or an exhaustively described analysis without qualifying output, using NR for silence and UNC for ambiguous evidence. Record inconsistency only from supplied evidence meeting the existing same-object, same-condition contradiction rule.

NOT_USED = the report states that the final model kept all candidate predictors or that no reduced model was built, or the only importance-related reduction is something else: a drop-out analysis (one predictor or category removed at a time to measure its contribution, e.g. ΔAUROC), a predictor dropped for a stated reason other than its importance (e.g. prevalence, leakage, clinical grounds), or importance-selected variables used only in descriptive or association analyses rather than in a prediction model. NR = the report says nothing about it. This includes studies that computed no importance or chose predictors by significance tests, stepwise selection or tree splitting, a reduced model mentioned only as future work, and prespecified candidate predictors or interpretation-only SHAP with no statement that all candidates stayed in the final model. round1.proposed_rule: The object of this item is the handling of real missing values in the predictor or outcome data relative to a train/test, resampling or validation structure. Imputation methods that are themselves the models being evaluated are not preprocessing for this item. Choose the code as follows. NA (status not_applicable): the study has no train/test, resampling or validation data. USED: the report states that every data-dependent missing-data step (fitted imputation, exclusion of variables by missingness rate) was fitted on training data only or within each fold, or the only stated handling fits nothing to the data. Examples of handling that fits nothing are complete-case exclusion of persons and coding missing values as a fixed constant. Do not assume missing values in variables the report does not mention. NOT_USED: the report states, or linked statements establish, that a data-dependent missing-data step used data that included the test or validation data (e.g. variables dropped by missingness rate on the whole dataset before the split or cross-validation; imputation fitted on all data). UNC: missing-data handling is stated, but either its data scope relative to the split cannot be fixed or the report shows that missing values remain whose handling is not stated. NR: the report states no missing-data handling; an exclusion that the report does not describe as due to missing data does not count. Status is reported for every code except NA.

Assess all explicitly described missing-data operations across the evaluated models, including imputation methods evaluated as comparators. Record-wise exclusions and fixed missing-value recoding may precede partitioning because they require no estimation across records; operations that estimate quantities across records, including variable filtering by sample missingness, must use training data alone within each relevant split or resample. Code NOT_USED if any stated operation violates this separation; otherwise code UNC if a stated operation's relevant procedure or data scope cannot be established, and USED if the stated operations satisfy separation or require no such estimation. Do not invent additional missingness or operations for variables whose handling is unmentioned. Code NR when missing-data handling is not stated; an unexplained eligibility or exclusion label does not establish it. Code NA only when the report establishes that the item has no object, including absence of a train/test or resampling structure by design; silence alone does not establish this. Data-dependent preprocessing includes both estimating preprocessing parameters and choosing transformations, cut-points or predictors using the study data; fixed formulas and prespecified exclusions alone do not qualify. round1.proposed_rule: Grade from what the report states about the final predictors. Y: for every final predictor the report gives a definition or a measurement source/procedure (question wording or response categories, named instrument, examination protocol, formula, single collection method, or a harmonised crosswalk) that applies to all participants, and the data come from one survey round, or the report states that the predictors were harmonised/comparable across the rounds or surveys pooled. PY: the predictors come from one stated standardised survey or dataset, but definitions or procedures are missing for some predictors, or several rounds are pooled with no statement on comparability, or some predictor values were assigned (matched, donor-imputed) rather than measured, as long as the report states no difference between participants. PN/N: the report states that definitions, instruments or procedures differed between groups of participants (rounds, sites, devices, sources): N when the difference is stated to affect the predictor values, PN when its effect is not stated. NI: only when the report states neither the source nor the definition of the predictors. A predictor source stated without procedural detail is PY, not NI. Give one entry per model and development dataset, and use 'all models | <dataset>' when the grade is the same for every model.

Assess each final or compared developed model using its own predictor set and stated development dataset; combine entries only when the same judgement applies. Code Y when reported common definitions and measurement procedures cover that predictor set across development participants, PY when affirmative evidence supports common assessment but leaves comparability partly uncertain, and NI when comparable assessment lacks supporting evidence: survey provenance, predictor lists, common encoding or format harmonisation alone are insufficient, whereas a described shared questionnaire, recall or measurement protocol can suffice without separate procedural detail for every variable. Code N or PN for stated or supported probable differences between participants, not merely incomplete reporting or conflicting descriptions. Apply inconsistency separately: conflicting definitions of the same predictor under the same conditions are present; omissions from an illustrative list are not contradictions; uncertain identity between descriptions warrants uncertain.

round1.proposed_rule: Code met only if an amount (count or percentage, printed or directly derivable from printed counts for that variable) is given for every variable, or named group of variables, that the report states had missing data. This covers the outcome and predictors, and includes those handled by imputation, by exclusion of incomplete cases, or flagged as containing missing values. Counts of participants excluded for nonresponse on a named variable, and 'no response' or 'missing' rows in a table, count as amounts for that variable. Also code met if the report states that there were no missing data. Code not_met if any variable stated to have missing data has no amount. Code not_met if the only figure is a total of complete or incomplete cases (e.g. cases missing 'some' or 'any' predictors), a missingness threshold, or the name of the imputation or exclusion method.

Code met when the report quantifies missingness or nonresponse for at least one identified variable, including an outcome, or a group with a stated common missingness pattern; reporting every predictor is not required. Qualifying evidence includes variable-specific exclusion counts, tabulated nonresponse counts, and explicitly linked eligible and responding counts for the same question, without requiring an unprinted missing count to be extracted. A handling method, exclusion policy or missingness threshold alone does not establish an amount; neither does a combined missingness/other-reason count establish the missingness component. Code not_met when no qualifying amount is stated; either response code has status reported.

Counts excluded for nonresponse on a named variable, 'no response'/'missing' rows in a table, and an amount computed from printed eligible and responding counts that the report gives for the same question all count as amounts. round1.proposed_rule: The core question is whether weights were combined across the pooled years. Code USED only when the report states a multi-year weight strategy applied to the pooled analysis: an integrated, combined or pooled weight, adjustment of yearly weights for the number of pooled years or cycles, or a weight variable that the report itself calls the multi-year weight. Use UNC only when it is ambiguous whether years were pooled, or when a combined-weight strategy is described but its use in the pooled analysis is unclear. Silence about weighting for one model (e.g. the ML model) when weights are stated elsewhere does not by itself make the code UNC.

USED means an explicit survey sampling-weight strategy was applied to an established pooled multi-year analysis; no particular year-count formula, separately named combined weight, or application to every model is required. round1.proposed_rule: Judge the three components against the validation that produced the reported performance estimates. (1) Internal-validation method: reported when the report states how the evaluation data were held out from model development: a train/test split (including a split by survey year or wave), cross-validation, or bootstrap. (2) Resampling details: reported when at least one parameter of that partition or resampling is printed: split proportion or sizes, number of folds, repeats or bootstrap samples, or the criterion that defines the split (e.g. survey years). Randomisation, stratification or a seed are not required. (3) Nesting of development steps: reported when, for every data-dependent development step the report describes (e.g. imputation, scaling or encoding fitted on data, outlier removal, class re-sampling, predictor selection, tuning, calibration, threshold choice), the report states which data the step used relative to that split or those folds. 'Before the split on all data', 'training set only' and 'within each fold' all count, whether the step was nested or not, because this item records what was done, not whether it was done well. Fitting the model itself on the training set does not count as a nesting statement. The nesting of inner tuning folds is not required. If the data scope of any described step is not stated, this component is not fully reported. R = all three components reported; P = one or two; NR = none, including studies with no validation or test data. List the reported components in the rationale.

Assign R only when all three components are reported, P when some are reported, and NR when none are reported; all three codes have status reported, with the reported components listed in the rationale. For resampling details, require the allocation for each evaluation split, the fold count for CV, and the resample or repetition count when repeated resampling is stated; randomisation, stratification and seed are not additional mandatory details. Nesting requires an explicit account of where the reported data-dependent development steps occurred relative to the evaluation split and applicable resampling loops; the validation method alone or the placement of only some stated steps is insufficient. Explicit placement outside a split or loop counts as reporting, regardless of methodological quality, but training-set use alone establishes neither refitting within CV folds nor execution outside them. Count tuning-only CV as resampling, not as validation of reported performance, and external validation alone supplies no internal-validation component. Infer neither procedures nor their absence from silence, and record inconsistency only for incompatible statements about the same object and condition, using uncertain only when potentially conflicting statements cannot be matched to the same object.

Code R when all three components are reported, P when one or two are, and NR when none is, including studies with no validation or test data. Status is reported for every code. round1.proposed_rule: Judge only the final or best model(s) the report presents as its result. Subgroup or comparator models do not lower the grade unless the report presents them as final. R: the report or supplement gives everything needed to compute a prediction for a new person. That means one of these: a full equation with every coefficient and the intercept or baseline; a complete tree with every split and every terminal-node class or probability; a complete score with its points and cut-off; a network with all of its prior and conditional probabilities, each tied by printed labels to its node and parent states; or a shared fitted model file, or code with the final hyperparameter values. P: some fitted content of the final model is printed, but not all of it. Examples are coefficients without an intercept, a tree with some terminal-node predictions missing, probabilities whose node or condition the printed labels do not fix, or chosen hyperparameter values without code or a file. NR: no fitted content of the final model is printed. Algorithm names, software, input or predictor lists, variable importance or SHAP, hyperparameter search ranges or grids without the chosen values, and descriptions of the modelling procedure do not count as specification. Do not assign printed values to nodes from their order or position alone. Record contradictions about the final model's coefficients, predictors or nodes under the existing inconsistency rule.

Code once for the study: R when every explicitly identified final prediction model is specified sufficiently to generate its intended predictions, through a complete equation, tree, score, shared model file, or full hyperparameters with code; P when at least one has application-defining components, such as fitted coefficients, branches, conditional probabilities or selected parameter values, but some necessary specification or final-model coverage is incomplete or ambiguous; NR when none has such components. Algorithm or software names, predictor lists, development procedures, search ranges, importance or SHAP results, and a calculator without model specification do not alone qualify as P. Require the labels, input coding and terminal outputs needed for application, without inferring missing components; do not require training details or internal-node statistics when the supplied prediction rule already determines the output. Apply the existing inconsistency rule separately: present requires contradictory statements about the same fact, object and condition, supported by IDs in the supplied input; uncertain applies only when the report leaves it uncertain whether the statements concern the same object, and otherwise use none when no contradiction is established.

round1.proposed_rule: Met when the report prints everything needed to compute a prediction for a new person from the final model(s), together with the definition (categories or cut-offs) of each input. For regression: the fitted coefficient or OR of every final predictor, plus the intercept, or a nomogram with points per category and a total-points-to-risk scale. For a tree: the complete tree as a diagram or rule table that shows, for every terminal node, the path of split variables with their categories or cut-offs and the node's predicted class or outcome rate. A printed tree diagram counts as printed rules when its splits and node values are printed in it. Not met: only selected nodes (e.g. high-risk paths), only variable names or importance, or generic equations with symbolic betas. When the final model has several parts (e.g. tree-defined strata with a regression in each), every part must be specified this way, otherwise not_met. For this item, inconsistency present only when the same coefficient, points value or tree node is printed differently in two places. Differences from descriptive tables, between significant-factor lists and model inputs, or involving approximate figure readings whose attribution to a term is not printed are not present (uncertain only when the report does not allow telling whether the same term or node is meant).

Read 'specifies the final model for new data' literally: met requires a stated specification connecting defined inputs to predictions, without inferring missing fitted quantities, tree connections or terminal predictions; generic equations, isolated split labels, selected paths and diagrams serving another purpose do not alone establish this. A nomogram supplies such a specification when its defined inputs, point assignments and total-points-to-prediction mapping are given. When the criterion has an object, code reported with met or not_met; use not_applicable only when that object does not exist by design. Assess inconsistency separately: require contradictory information about the same fact, object and condition, use uncertain when their identity cannot be established, and do not treat rounding as a contradiction or change reporting status because values disagree.

round1.proposed_rule: C35 is met when the report explicitly states the availability status of the study data and who holds or releases them. Examples: 'publicly available from/released by <agency>', 'available to the public', 'available on reasonable request from <person or body>', or a stated reason why sharing is restricted. A URL, repository or step-by-step access procedure is not required. C35 is not_met when the report only names or describes the data source, or only says it used KNHANES data released or conducted by an agency, and says nothing about whether the data can be accessed. Statements about de-identification, IRB exemption or data governance do not by themselves state availability.

Code met when the report states whether the study data are available and how they can be accessed, or explains why sharing is restricted. Stating that data are publicly available or open-source and naming their source or releasing agency, without an access location or procedure, is not_met. Do not infer access details that the report does not state.

rule_source: agreed by both systems in round 2
final_rule: Code met when the report states whether the study data are available and how they can be accessed, or explains why sharing is restricted. Stating that data are publicly available or open-source and naming their source or releasing agency, without an access location or procedure, is not_met. Do not infer access details that the report does not state.

round1.proposed_rule: This item covers only the step that combines participant-level importance into an overall value (for example, mean |SHAP|). Code USED only when the report states that survey weights were applied in that step. Examples: a weighted mean of |SHAP|, or an explicit statement that the importance summary was weighted to the population. Survey weights used in an earlier step do not make this item USED, and neither does averaging over a split taken from weighted data. Earlier steps include resampling, duplicating or rebalancing the dataset, weighted training, and weighted performance metrics. Record those earlier uses in the rationale only. Code NOT_USED only when the report states that the importance was aggregated without weights. If the report gives a plain average (for example, 'averaged over the test set') and says nothing about weights at that step, code NR. Code NA when no participant-level importance method was used.

Code only what the report states or cited statements logically establish about survey-weight use in aggregating participant-level importance. Survey-weight use in another step alone does not establish USED for this item. When participant-level importance exists but its aggregation weighting is unstated, code NR with status reported; an unspecified average establishes neither USED nor NOT_USED.

round1.proposed_rule: met requires four printed elements: the source sample size, the eligibility criteria, a number excluded for every exclusion reason or restriction the report states, and the final analytic sample. One printed count is enough for reasons the report applies together as a single step. not_met when any stated reason or restriction has no printed count, either its own or a joint one; do not infer a missing count (e.g. zero) from the arithmetic of the other counts. not_met also when the printed exclusion count contradicts the source and final counts so the number excluded cannot be fixed; record this as inconsistency present as well. Exclusion counts that do not sum to source minus final, where the report does not say whether the steps are sequential or overlapping, do not prevent met; record them as inconsistency uncertain. A count stated for an intermediate step (e.g. a count stated after an age criterion was applied) is a different object from the final sample, not an inconsistency. A threshold written as a fraction in one place and as a percent in another is notation.

Code met when the source size, eligibility criteria, final analytic size, and exclusion reasons with counts are stated, or exclusions are explicitly stated not to have occurred. Every stated participant-exclusion reason must have a linked printed count; one count explicitly covering several reasons suffices. Reconciled totals do not establish a count, zero exclusions, or overlap for an otherwise uncounted reason. Judge reporting, not numerical agreement: contradictions are recorded separately and do not make reported components missing. Record inconsistency only for contradictory information about the same fact, object and condition; omitted counts, different selection stages, and arithmetic conflicts requiring unstated assumptions about overlapping or disjoint exclusions do not establish a contradiction.

final_rule:
Code met when the source sample size, eligibility criteria and final analytic sample size are stated, and every stated exclusion reason or restriction has a linked printed count (one count explicitly covering several reasons suffices), or exclusions are explicitly stated not to have occurred; otherwise code not_met. The source size, eligibility criteria and final size are required in either case; never calculate a missing exclusion count or infer zero exclusions.

- If an exclusion count contradicts the source and final counts for the same sample under the stated selection relationships, so the number excluded cannot be fixed, code not_met and inconsistency present.

round1.proposed_rule: The item has an object whenever the report ranks variables or names some of them as most important, main, major or influential, whether in text, tables or figures. Code not_applicable only when the report does neither. Code met when the report states the criterion that orders or selects these variables and that criterion applies to them. Examples of such a criterion: importance score, odds ratio, nomogram points, or 'selected stepwise by size of influence/impurity reduction'. Code met also when the report prints the ordering statistic for every variable in the model, so that the full order can be read from printed values. Code not_met when variables are named as important or listed in order, but no criterion is stated and the statistic is not printed for all variables. Judge only whether a criterion is reported, not whether it is a good one. Contradictory values of that statistic go under inconsistency and do not change met.

Code met for a full reported ranking or a stated criterion explicitly linked to identifying or ordering the most influential variables, including influence-based predictor selection during model construction; no additional top-k or cutoff is required. Scores or a partial list alone do not suffice: do not infer an ordering, a selection criterion, or aggregation across variable levels. Missing ranking/rule reporting warrants reported/not_met, unless the stated-reason exception applies; reserve not_applicable for an object absent by design.
