round1.proposed_rule: Assess the uncertainty printed for the prediction-model results (CIs, SEs or SDs of performance or of model coefficients). If none is printed for them, assess the study's other inferential analyses (SEs, CIs, significance tests). Code NA (status not_applicable) only when no CI, SE, SD of an estimate, p-value or test is printed anywhere. Descriptive mean ± SD and point estimates alone do not count. USED: the report states that strata and clusters/PSUs (or an equivalent design-based method, e.g. complex-samples procedure, replicate weights) were applied to the assessed analysis. NOT_USED: the assessed analysis uses a named variance method that is not survey-based and has no strata or PSU stated (e.g. robust or HC SEs, DeLong, bootstrap of individuals, cross-validation fold SD, ordinary tests), or the report states that the survey design was not applied to it. UNC: a survey-type method is named but the report does not state that strata or PSUs were applied in it (e.g. 'weighted' or 'Rao-Scott for weighted samples' only); weights alone never make USED. NR: uncertainty values are printed for the assessed analysis but no method is stated. Design handling of analyses that were not assessed goes in the rationale only.

Assess uncertainty estimation and inferential tests anywhere in the study, including descriptive and association analyses. Code USED if at least one such analysis explicitly accounts for strata and clusters or uses an equivalent survey-design method; identify that analysis in the rationale without extending its design handling to other analyses. Otherwise, code NOT_USED only when design-ignorant variance estimation is explicitly established, UNC when a reported variance method leaves its design components or analysis linkage unclear, and NR when the variance method is unreported. A conventional method name, generic bootstrap description, sampling-design description or omission of weights does not by itself establish NOT_USED. Code NA only when the report establishes that no applicable uncertainty analysis exists; absent uncertainty outputs alone support NR. Use only the supplied report text, not unsupported descriptions in coder rationales.

round3_candidates.P: Assess uncertainty estimation and inferential tests anywhere in the study, including descriptive and association analyses. round1.proposed_rule: Code how missing predictor values were handled in the main prediction analysis. Code other_or_several only when the main prediction analysis applies methods from different categories to missing predictor values (e.g. deletes some records with missing predictors and imputes others). round1.proposed_rule: The criterion has an object only when the report states that importance was computed per participant (per observation) and then summarised across participants. Examples: SHAP or mean |SHAP| summary or beeswarm plots, LIME, or other local explanations that are averaged. Do not code not_met because the method is unclear. Code met or not_met only when participant-level aggregation is stated: met if the report says whether and how survey weights were used in that aggregation (a stated reason for not using them also counts), otherwise not_met.

round1.proposed_rule: Assign components by classifying each outcome or predictor variable that the report names anywhere (text, tables, figures, variable codes) by how the report says it was obtained. Physical measurements such as anthropometry, BMI and blood pressure go to EXAMINATION. Blood or urine tests go to LABORATORY. The dentist's oral examination goes to ORAL_HEALTH. Dietary intake or food/nutrient data go to NUTRITION. Lab tests and the oral exam are coded only as LABORATORY or ORAL_HEALTH, even when the report files them under the health examination. round1.proposed_rule: A sample-size rationale is a statement that justifies why the number of participants or outcome events used to develop or evaluate the reported models is large enough. Examples are a formal calculation, minimum sample-size criteria, events-per-variable, a learning-curve check, or an explicit argument that the sample is adequate. These do not count and are coded NR: descriptions of how the sample was formed (all eligible survey participants, inclusion or exclusion steps, down-sampling or oversampling to balance classes, split sizes), and remarks that some sample was too small for an analysis or outcome that was then dropped. Put such remarks in the rationale. The item has one component, so the code is R if such a rationale is stated and NR if not. As with any legacy code, NR has status 'reported' and must cite at least one evidence ID: the passage that describes the sample source or size, or the passage that was checked.

Count as a sample-size rationale an explicit explanation of how or why the analysis sample size was determined, or an explicit assessment of sample-size adequacy that informed an analysis decision. This includes a class-balancing rule that determines the included sample size and stated sample-size insufficiency that motivates a change in analysis; sample counts, survey descriptions and eligibility criteria alone do not qualify. Code R when either a rationale or a calculation is reported, identifying the component in the rationale; a formal calculation or demonstration of statistical adequacy is not additionally required. Code NR when neither is reported, retaining status reported and the existing citation requirements without inferring that all eligible participants were used.

round1.proposed_rule: Component 1 is met by either (a) a complete specification of the fitted final model, from which a reader could compute the output for a new person (e.g. all coefficients with intercept, or a tree diagram or rule list giving every split variable, cut-point or category grouping, and the predicted proportion or class at every terminal node), or (b) an executable artefact that the report states is available (e.g. deployed calculator or web app, downloadable model file or code). Either one alone meets component 1. Partial material does not: structure without parameters, hyperparameters, variable importance, or code 'available on request'. Component 2 (use instructions) is met only by text that tells a user how to apply the final model to one person: which inputs to enter or measure and how to get and read the predicted output. Recommendations about whom to target or what to assess, implications for practice, interpretation of the results, demonstrations (e.g. what-if analyses), and interface screenshots or captions without such steps do not count. Code R when both components are met, P when one is, and NR when neither is. Name the components that were met in the rationale, and cite at least one evidence ID even for NR.

Assess two components separately: (1) a complete specification sufficient to reproduce the fitted final model's predictions without refitting, or a reported executable implementation of that model; (2) instructions explaining how to apply it and obtain or read its prediction. A complete tree with branch conditions and terminal predictions or a reported deployed prediction application can establish the first component; network structure, hyperparameters or availability of analytical code alone cannot. Use instructions may be textual or illustrated, including an input/output interface or directions to follow a tree from root to terminal output; merely displaying pathways, describing subgroup or hypothetical results, or recommending screening, intervention or future implementation does not establish them. Code R when both components are reported, P when one is reported and NR when neither is reported; list the reported components and their evidence in the rationale, with only the response code in the value.

round1.proposed_rule: The object of this item is an importance analysis: the report presents importance values or a ranking of the predictors, from built-in (impurity, gain, Gini, relative influence), permutation, SHAP or other attribution methods. If the report has none, the status is not_applicable. Descriptions of the splitting criterion used to grow a tree, and overall correlations of the inputs with the outcome, are not importance analyses. When an importance analysis exists, the status is reported and the value is decided per method used, as follows. The value is met when, for each method, the report states the settings that define that method's importance computation: for built-in importance, the importance type (e.g. gain, mean impurity decrease, feature_importances_ of the named model) and any stated repetition or averaging; for permutation importance, the performance metric and the number of repeats; for SHAP or other explainers, the explainer type and the background data (its size or source). The value is not_met when only the method name is given ('SHAP', 'variable importance') without these settings. Fitted-model hyperparameters, seeds, how the background sample was selected, and software versions are not required for met. Their absence goes in the rationale.

Assess settings specific to calculating importance, without requiring the full model-fitting recipe: naming a built-in importance measure or software attribute suffices when no additional importance computation is described. For additional computations, require the stated method-specific choices, data sources and sampling procedures, and any repetition and aggregation procedure; background size alone does not specify background selection, and a repetition count alone does not specify how importance results are combined. Do not supply missing choices from assumed defaults. Missing required settings, or silence about importance, yields reported/not_met; not_applicable requires affirmative evidence that the criterion has no object by design. A stated reason for omitting the calculation may meet the criterion as its definition allows.

If that is the only interpretation and no separate importance or explanation method is applied, code NA (status not_applicable). Code USED only when the text describes a step that compares the explanation with the explained model's behaviour and presents it as a check of the explanation, for example perturbing or removing the top-ranked variables of that model, or comparing explanation methods on the same model. None of the following is a fidelity check: agreement with clinical knowledge or the literature; comparison with rankings from a different model; an ablation or retraining that is itself the importance method or is used to select predictors; a fidelity statistic printed automatically in a figure that the text does not describe or use. Code NOT_USED only when the report states that the explanation's fidelity was not checked. A general call for further validation is not such a statement, so code NR in that case and whenever an explanation method exists but no check is reported.

Displaying or interpreting a fitted tree’s own splits and paths alone does not count as an importance/explanation method; use NA (status not_applicable) when VI01 is not USED. Otherwise, code USED for a reported comparison assessing agreement between an explanation and the explained model’s behaviour; a labelled explanation-fit value in a figure suffices without narrative discussion, whereas clinical plausibility or similar rankings across different models do not. Ablation that merely generates importance rankings, or reduced-model comparisons used only to select predictors, does not establish a fidelity check: the report must also show a comparison checking the explanation against model behaviour. Use NOT_USED only when non-performance is explicitly stated or logically established; otherwise use NR, including when validation is merely said to remain necessary, with status reported for either code.

round1.proposed_rule: Code Y when the report states that the outcome was formed by cutting a recorded score, index, lab value, measurement or numeric count or duration, or states that a categorical outcome is derived from such a named score, index or measurement. In that second case the cut-off value need not be printed. Code UNC when the report says only that some parts of the outcome came from examinations or measurements, without naming the measure or saying how it was used. A frequency, duration, count or time-window limit that is part of the wording of a yes/no definition gives N, unless the report states that the underlying number was recorded and then cut. When the model is fitted to a continuous value or numeric score, code NA, even if thresholds are applied afterwards to its predictions or nodes. Record an inconsistency only when places in the report conflict on how the outcome was formed. A conflicting outcome name belongs to the outcome-definition items.

Code Y when the report explicitly defines outcome membership using a quantitative or ordered cut-off, including duration or event count, alone or within a composite definition; questionnaire origin does not exclude Y, and a separately recorded numerical variable need not be inferred. Eligibility restrictions and observation windows alone do not count. Apply this to the modeled outcome: subsequent grouping of continuous predictions does not change NA, and numerical scales or evaluation metrics alone do not establish target type. Code N for an explicitly stated construction from categorical responses without stated quantitative categorisation, and UNC when construction remains unresolved; never supply thresholds from an index name, named criteria or examination provenance. Record inconsistency only when supplied statements contradict the same fact about the same object under the same condition.

round1.proposed_rule: Y only if at least one interval estimate (CI bounds, SD, SE or IQR across resamples) is printed for a model performance measure (text, table cell or a value printed in a figure). A statement that intervals were computed or are shown, with no printed interval value, is N: quote the statement in the rationale. Intervals for non-performance quantities (e.g. SHAP values, odds ratios, predictor statistics) do not count. Inconsistency for this item concerns only the fact the code rests on, i.e. whether an interval estimate is reported and what kind it is (e.g. the same interval called CI in one place and SD in another). Contradictory performance values or interval bounds, point estimates outside their interval, and differences in how a split is named belong to the performance items, not to this code: inconsistency none for these. A statement that intervals are given while none are printed is not an inconsistency: code N and explain in the rationale.

Code Y when numerical interval bounds or an explicitly identified numerical uncertainty estimate, such as a standard deviation, are printed for at least one performance measure of a final or compared model, including in supplementary material. A statement that intervals were calculated or accompany results, without numerical uncertainty values, is insufficient: code N when performance is evaluated but no qualifying value is printed, and NA only when no performance evaluation exists; legacy status is reported for Y/N and not_applicable for NA. Apply the existing inconsistency rule: present requires two supplied passages contradicting the same fact, object and condition; uncertain applies when potentially conflicting passages cannot be established as referring to the same object. Different analyses, different statistics, rounding and unsupported assertions of discrepancies do not establish present.

round1.proposed_rule: Y = the report names a statistical test, or prints a p-value or an interval, for a performance difference between two or more models evaluated in the study (including nested models, e.g. base vs base + predictor), whether or not the test accounts for pairing on the same patients or folds (e.g. DeLong, McNemar, bootstrap difference, paired t-test, or ANOVA with post-hoc pairwise tests on fold scores); whether the test is appropriate is risk of bias, not extraction. UNC = no such test or value is printed, but the report says a difference between models is statistically significant (in the text or a table note). N = two or more models are evaluated and compared only by point estimates, with no claim of significance. NA = performance is reported for only one model; tuning candidates and other studies' results do not count as evaluated models. Code the study by the highest level present (Y > UNC > N).

Code NA when only one model is evaluated in the study; comparisons with published studies do not count as additional evaluated models. Otherwise, code Y only when a formal between-model performance comparison is reported and pairing is stated or established by the named procedure. Code N when no such comparison is reported: pairwise post-hoc results, shared evaluation folds, significance notes and claims of significant improvement alone do not establish paired analysis. Use UNC only when affirmative descriptions of a performance comparison are ambiguous or conflicting about pairing; omission of pairing information alone is N. N describes nonreporting, not proof that paired testing was not performed.

round1.proposed_rule: Use the same method-focused or health-focused classification as legacy.method_stages. A study counts as method-focused when the report presents a technique as its contribution (labelled proposed, new or enhanced) and compares it with the results without it; a stated aim of building a risk model does not override this. Assign the first category that applies, in the order listed. A held-out split of the study's own KNHANES data, whether random or by survey year, is never an independent dataset, even if the report calls it independent or external. A comparator is a named method whose results are compared with the proposed method's, including the same model without the proposed step. Two things are not comparators: candidate algorithms compared to choose a component of the method, and reruns of the method with swapped components to test consistency.

Treat a study as method-focused when it explicitly presents and evaluates a method or modification as a methodological contribution, even when it also has a health prediction objective. A qualifying comparator evaluates that contribution against a named alternative or baseline, including the method without the proposed modification; algorithm selection within the method and component substitutions used only to assess robustness or consistency do not themselves qualify. Choose the first supported category in the listed order; an explicitly independent evaluation dataset can come from the same survey, whereas a held-out split of the development dataset is not external. Use SINGLE_EMPIRICAL_APPLICATION when the described evaluation establishes application without a qualifying comparator, and EVALUATION_DESIGN_INSUFFICIENTLY_REPORTED when the design cannot be fixed from the text. Apply the existing inconsistency rule: present requires contradictory statements about the same fact, object and condition; differing non-exhaustive comparator mentions or omitted result rows do not establish a contradiction.

round1.proposed_rule: Focus: method-focused only when the report states its aim or contribution as a method, framework or approach (proposed, improved or compared) that KNHANES is used to demonstrate or evaluate. If the stated objective is a prediction or risk model, or risk factors, for a health outcome, the study is health-focused (not_applicable), even if preprocessing or ML techniques are applied to improve that model. Stages: code only the stages that the title, abstract, aims, contribution statements or the text's description of the proposed method's steps present as components of the method being developed, improved or compared. Do not code steps the study only performs when applying it (deleting records or features with missing values, standard cross-validation or split, standard metrics, comparison with baselines, a flowchart box without such a statement). MISSING_DATA, VALIDATION_OR_PERFORMANCE_EVALUATION and EXPLAINABLE_AI need a missing-data, evaluation or interpretability procedure that the report presents as part of the method (e.g. its own evaluation scheme; feature importance or a nomogram given as the method's interpretability component), not the choice of existing metrics. USER_TOOL_OR_WORKFLOW only when software, an app, a web tool or a decision-support system is delivered as a contribution; a multi-step framework is coded by its stages, and a nomogram or scoring chart is EXPLAINABLE_AI.

Apply the existing applicability rule: the main contribution must concern developing, improving or comparing a method, workflow or tool; describing a disease-prediction pipeline alone does not establish method focus. For applicable studies, include every stage explicitly performed in the described method/workflow or its evaluation, whether conventional or novel, rather than only its headline contribution. Classify stages by their stated function: removal because of missingness counts as MISSING_DATA, and explicitly performed validation or performance assessment counts as VALIDATION_OR_PERFORMANCE_EVALUATION without requiring a new evaluation method. USER_TOOL_OR_WORKFLOW requires an explicitly constructed tool or an analysis workflow explicitly presented as a contribution; the word 'framework' or possible future extension alone is insufficient, software is not required, and the same artifact may also receive EXPLAINABLE_AI when its explanatory function is stated.

final_rule:

round1.proposed_rule: Code only the selection or exclusion criteria that the report states the study applied to the KNHANES participants it analysed. Do not code criteria of other (non-KNHANES) cohorts in the same report. Do not code exclusions printed as part of the survey's own measurement protocol; if the study requires that measurement, code MEASUREMENT_OR_DATA_AVAILABILITY. Do not code descriptive labels of the population (e.g. 'at high risk of X') unless a criterion or exclusion step is stated for them. Selection or sampling by outcome class (balanced case/control draws, keeping only some outcome categories, dropping outcome levels for a model) is outcome sampling, not a restriction; record it in the rationale. A stated rule that fits no category (e.g. occupation, employment) is not DISEASE_OR_RISK_GROUP. If none of the stated rules fits a category, status is not_reported and the rule goes in the rationale. For this item, inconsistency is present only when two places state the restriction itself differently (e.g. different age limits). Count mismatches in the participant flow are not inconsistencies of this item.

Record the union of stated restrictions across analysed cohorts and model-specific participant subsets in one study-level entry, identifying their scope in the rationale. Selection by a stated health condition or risk group includes outcome-based subsampling or balancing and does not require a printed operational cutoff; stated measurement-safety exclusions also apply when the text establishes that the analysis requires that measurement. Add OTHER for explicitly stated restrictions outside the listed categories, describing their basis in the rationale; do not infer a health restriction from occupation, and reserve not_reported for absence of any stated selection rule. Apply the existing inconsistency rule to the same fact, population and condition: sample-count discrepancies alone do not contradict restriction codes, different cohorts' restrictions do not conflict, and contradictory age limits for the same analysed population do.

round1.proposed_rule: Judge the role by where the analysed participants or records come from, not by where the variables come from. If every participant or record on which models are developed and reported comes from KNHANES, code PRIMARY_ANALYSIS_DATASET. This applies even when data from another source are linked, matched, merged or 'integrated' into those records only as extra variables (features, area-level or condition-matched values). Code ONE_OF_MULTIPLE_PRIMARY_DATASETS only when the report states that participants or records from another source are themselves analysed: in a parallel analysis, or pooled with KNHANES rows for development. Naming another source as used, without stating that any analysed sample, analysis or result comes from it, does not count; mention it in the rationale. Code UNCLEAR only when the cited text does not show whether the other source contributes analysed participants or records.

Code ONE_OF_MULTIPLE_PRIMARY_DATASETS when the report explicitly states that KNHANES and another dataset were combined to form the data used for the main development or analysis, including combination by features; separate populations or separate analyses are not required. Do not infer that an expressly used source was unused or merely auxiliary from a KNHANES sample label or the absence of separate results. A nonexclusive attribution to KNHANES does not by itself contradict an explicit joint-use statement.
